We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincaré manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.

title: The Reaction of Financial Markets to the Releases of DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K3: A Critical Analysis
authors: Marco Taboga
abstract: This paper compares financial-market reactions to the releases of DeepSeek R1 in January 2025 and Kimi K3 in July 2026. Both AI models were presented as credible Chinese competitors near the capability frontier, but their releases conveyed different economic information. DeepSeek R1 combined open weights with unusually low reported training and inference costs, prompting investors to reassess expected demand for computing infrastructure and producing large stock-price decreases among semiconductor and data-centre-related firms. Kimi K3 instead entered at broadly frontier prices and generated a market reaction concentrated more heavily among rival Chinese AI laboratories. Drawing on descriptive event-window evidence, model capability and cost comparisons, subsequent industry developments, and the historical diffusion of open-source software, the paper argues that open-weight models redistribute rents across the AI value chain rather than eliminating them. Incumbents remain protected by complementary assets including distribution, product bundling, switching costs, proprietary data, serving capacity, and contractual trust. The analysis suggests that investors and policy makers should assess risks looking not only at model capability, but also at the ownership and durability of complementary assets across the AI value chain.

title: From Perpetrators' Digital Footprints to Behavioral Communities: An Ontology-Driven Framework for Bengali Cyberbullying Analysis--- FULL VERSION
authors: Md. Nesarul Hoque, Md Hanif Seddiqui, Miskatul Anwara, Rudra Pratap Deb Nath
abstract: Cyberbullying involves behavioral and contextual patterns beyond isolated abusive messages. However, existing approaches remain fragmented across content detection, semantic representation, and network analysis, with limited interpretable perpetrator representations, multi-scale structural modeling, and explanations of behavior-driven similarity and influence propagation. These limitations hinder the identification of persistent perpetrators, characterization of behavioral communities, and assessment of potentially influential users. This paper proposes Ontology-Driven Cyberbullying Behavior and Network Analysis (ODCBNA), a perpetrator-centric framework integrating requirements-driven ontology design, knowledge graph construction, behavioral modeling, community analysis, and influence modeling. Using the Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying (BenCoDiC) corpus as a use case, ODCBNA identifies $1{,}063$ users with at least three bullying comments or replies as perpetrators and represents each through a $64$-dimensional behavioral and contextual feature vector. Cosine similarity and $k$-nearest-neighbor modeling produce a weighted network with $27{,}554$ edges. Louvain analysis identifies six communities with a modularity of approximately $0.495$ and $27$ sub-communities. Feature-contribution analysis identifies the Video, Impact, and User Profile groups as the strongest contributors to behavioral similarity and community separation, while contextual dimensions support interpretation. Community-constrained influence analysis shows that IM Greedy achieves small positive gains in all six communities, although different seed-selection methods produce comparable diffusion spreads despite limited seed overlap. These findings provide an interpretable basis for understanding perpetrator behavior, community organization, and potential influence patterns in Bengali online environments.

title: Spectral and edge conditions for negative Hamiltonian cycles in unbalanced signed graphs
authors: Zihao Zha
abstract: Spectral conditions for Hamiltonian cycles are a fundamental subject in extremal spectral graph theory. For simple unsigned graphs, Fiedler and Nikiforov [Linear Algebra Appl., 432 (2010), 2170-2173] pioneered this direction, and Li and Ning [Linear Multilinear Algebra, 64 (2016), 2252-2269] later extended these results by introducing minimum degree parameters. In this paper, we study the spectral conditions for the existence of a negative Hamiltonian cycle in unbalanced signed graphs of order n > 8. We first determine the maximum index among all n-vertex unbalanced signed graphs containing no negative Hamiltonian cycle, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs up to switching isomorphism. Furthermore, we establish an upper bound on the number of edges in unbalanced signed graphs of order n >= 7 with frustration index one, and classify all extremal graphs achieving this bound.

title: ATLAS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Lifting Binary to Canonical Compiler IR
authors: Xiaoao Zhu, Ni Zhang, Jie Ren, Zhiqiang Li, Jie Zheng, Zhanyong Tang, Zheng Wang
abstract: Lifting stripped, heavily optimized binaries to a canonical, pre-optimization LLVM intermediate representation (IR) is essential for downstream security analysis and legacy software migration when source code is unavailable. However, aggressive compiler optimizations rewrite control and data flow, remove structural metadata, and introduce type-erased low-level idioms, causing current lifters to produce malformed or semantically divergent IR. We present ATLAS, a multi-agent framework designed to reconstruct formally valid and canonical LLVM IR from optimized disassembly.ATLAS combines (i) Structure-aware, region-level retrieval, which utilizes pseudo-probe attribution to align optimized instructions with canonical IR exemplars, and (ii) a collaborative refinement loop that closes the gap between probabilistic generation and deterministic compiler constraints. Concretely, a Lift agent generates an initial IR draft conditioned on retrieved exemplars, an Advisor agent interprets LLVM verifier/compilation diagnostics and static checks to propose localized repair actions, and a Validation agent applies the edits, re-runs toolchain verification and (when available) runtime checks, and feeds the resulting diagnostics back to the Advisor. The agents iterate until the IR is verifier-clean and behaviorally consistent, or a budget limit is reached. On HumanEval-Decompile and MBPP, ATLAS outperforms seven baselines on lifting LLVM IR, achieving 91.8% re-executability and 89.4% CFG similarity across ARM, x86-64, and RISC-V binaries. Moreover, our evaluation demonstrates that ATLAS also outperforms the Binary to C to IR pipelines in pointer-flow precision and downstream analyzability. By recovering a well-formed, machine-centric representation, ATLAS enables practical cross-ISA recompilation and verifiable binary-only migration workflows.

title: Lip-Focused Audio-Visual Consistency Detects Speech Content Manipulation beyond Coarse Synchronization
authors: Jian Zong, Chenghan Lin, Meng Liu, Zhao Xu, Junyu Wang, Siyuan Zhang, Peiyuan Jiang, Longbiao Wang, Jianwu Dang
abstract: Speech-content manipulation changes what a visible person appears to say by replacing the speech track and, in stronger attacks, regenerating mouth motion to match the forged utterance. Such attacks are difficult to expose with texture artifacts or coarse lip-sync scores because modern retalking models explicitly optimize audio-visual synchrony. We test the narrower hypothesis that speech replacement still perturbs the local relationship between acoustic dynamics and mouth motion after speaker identity or coarse synchrony is controlled. To isolate this signal, we introduce SyncSpeech, an LRS3-derived benchmark containing real videos, audio-splicing cheapfakes and Wav2Lip retalking attacks under same-speaker and different-speaker replacement. We then introduce C-MIND, a lip-focused detector that aligns audio and mouth-motion representations at frame level and models their agreement and disagreement without transcripts, automatic speech recognition features or an unmanipulated reference. On SyncSpeech, pretrained SyncLip-C achieves 95.813% scenario-averaged accuracy and 0.9943 AUC, outperforming sentence-level fusion, full-face inputs and a reproduced SyncNet baseline under the reported protocol. When trained on the corresponding FakeAVCeleb training split, C-MIND correctly classifies 278 of 280 samples in the selected unseen-speaker test subset, whereas accuracy falls to 82.775% on unseen Video-Retalking attacks. These results identify lip-focused speech-articulation consistency as a useful but generator-sensitive forensic signal within the evaluated settings.

title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
authors: Zhuoran Zhang, Yang Shi, Qixun Wang, Tengfei Liu, Yuqi Tang, Xuanyu Zhu, Yizhuo Jia, Jingyun Hua, Shixuan Liu, Xianghua Ying, Haotian Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Wenjing Yang
abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection. Existing artifact-based detectors typically identify generation artifacts as evidence for source prediction, yet they may either fail to recognize subtle artifacts or reach the correct source decision without faithfully identifying the evidence underlying it. In this work, we systematically investigate how to design and train effective artifact detectors and formulate artifact detection as a structured process comprising three complementary capabilities: Inspection Planning, which determines what should be examined; Evidence Verification, which verifies whether the inspected content exhibits genuine generation artifacts; and Evidence Aggregation, which integrates the verified evidence into the final source decision. Building on this formulation, we introduce Verus-Insight, trained with human-anchored full-process supervision and progressive capability training to strengthen both fine-grained artifact detection and video-level detection. We further introduce Verus-Bench, a benchmark with fine-grained human annotations of perceptible artifacts for evaluating artifact detection. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that Verus-Insight achieves strong performance in both fine-grained artifact analysis and AI-generated video detection, with substantial gains in recovering human-perceived artifacts. Further analyses reveal that the three capabilities are complementary yet distinct, and that Verus-Insight more reliably converts relevant inspection targets into supported artifact evidence without increasing spurious artifact claims.

title: Consensus-Based Distributed Filtering for Angles-Only Tracking in Cislunar Space
authors: Giovanni Romagnoli, Fabrizio Pilone, Giordana Bucchioni
abstract: This paper investigates consensus-based distributed filtering strategies for multi-observer angles-only navigation in the cislunar space. The objective is to estimate the inertial state of a target spacecraft using only line-of-sight measurements collected by a network of observer spacecraft. This problem is particularly relevant for autonomous cislunar navigation, where ground support may be limited, and centralized fusion architectures may be problematic due to communication and computational constraints, and single-point failure risks. Three distributed filtering approaches are considered: the Distributed Extended Kalman Filter, the Information-Weighted Consensus Filter, and the Kalman Consensus Filter. All methods share the same local prediction and measurement-processing steps, but differ in the way information is exchanged and fused across the network. Their performance is evaluated and compared to a centralized Extended Kalman Filter, adopted as benchmark, and independent local filters in a high-fidelity cislunar scenario. Numerical simulations show that the distributed approaches significantly improve estimation accuracy with respect to independent filters. Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses are then conducted to characterize the robustness of the considered methods to finite consensus iterations and prior misalignment among the agents.

title: Cross-Spectral Feature Fusion for Multispectral Document Binarization
authors: Yasas Savinda, Maheshi Buddhinee Dissanayake
abstract: Historical document binarization remains challenging when faded ink, bleed-through, and background degradation exhibit wavelength-dependent behavior across visible and near-infrared observations. This study investigates whether adaptive cross-spectral feature fusion and targeted structural guidance can improve multispectral document binarization beyond fixed fusion and generic attention mechanisms. Four registered SMADI bands at 500, 600, 700, and 1000 nm are processed using a multi-branch conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). Visible, NIR, and structural feature streams are fused at encoder depth L = 3 using spatial- and channel-wise softmax gating, while auxiliary edge maps derived from selected VIS-NIR band pairs provide targeted structural guidance. Nine controlled fusion and structural configurations are evaluated using five-fold document-level cross-validation, DIBCO-standard metrics, and Holm-corrected statistical testing. The F3 + NIR edge-guided configuration provides the strongest overall performance among the evaluated models, achieving mean F1 = 0.7916, p-FM = 0.8044, and IoU = 0.6654. Relative to the fixed Mid AVG baseline, it improves F1 by 0.0269, p-FM by 0.0360, and IoU by 0.0321, with all three gains remaining statistically significant after Holm correction. Mean NRM and DRD are also reduced, although these reductions are not statistically significant after correction. Targeted cross-spectral structural guidance provides an effective mechanism for regulating intermediate multispectral fusion, improving primary foreground-overlap performance while retaining the complete four-band observation.

title: System-Level Evaluation of Uplink Access Schemes for Ambient IoT
authors: Douglas Dziedzorm Agbeve, Henrique Duarte Moura, Andrey Belogaev, Jeroen Famaey
abstract: Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT) devices operate under stringent energy constraints, relying on harvested power in the $μ$W-to-mW range and limited energy storage. The A-IoT air interface for active devices is still under development; we therefore use Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT) as an implementable reference for evaluating autonomous Uplink (UL) access under harvested energy. Under these conditions, the standard NB-IoT contention-based Random Access (RA) procedure incurs substantial per-packet overhead, making UL access in dense A-IoT networks increasingly energy-expensive. Context-retaining UL access schemes reduce this overhead, but their energy-latency trade-offs are insufficiently studied in literature under realistic harvesting and protocol constraints. To address this gap, we extend the LENA-NB ns-3 module with solar energy harvesting, supercapacitor storage, and a hysteretic brown-out mechanism, and propose Hybrid Scheduling Request (HSR), a hybrid UL access scheme combining reserved request occasions with opportunistic contention. We compare RA, Scheduling Request (SR), HSR and an Idealized Fast Uplink Grant (FUG) serving as a performance bound. Results show that HSR reduces mean packet delay by up to 69% and SR reduces energy per delivered bit by up to 24%, both relative to RA.

title: Lean Finder V2: Semantic Search for Mathlib That Disambiguates User Queries
authors: Jialin Lu, Xiaoyu Liu, Hengrui Luo, Rodrigo Stehling, Linxi Liu, Weiran Sun, Yuepeng Wang, Wuyang Chen
abstract: We introduce Lean Finder V2, a semantic search framework for Mathlib that disambiguates user queries through complementary model-level adversarial training and input-level query rewriting. Human mathematicians and coding agents rarely search Mathlib by providing detailed context. In practice, they query short properties, notation, aliases, or hypotheses, leaving much of the intended mathematics implicit. In contrast, existing Mathlib search engines unrealistically assume context-rich queries. The scarcity of real-world short queries paired with ground-truth Mathlib statements makes this ambiguity even more intractable. We argue that this is essentially a data problem. Through adversarial training, we scale up the generation of labeled short and ambiguous queries, and learn to disambiguate user queries at both model-level fine-tuning and input-level query rewriting. On the human-curated MathlibQR benchmark, our Lean Finder V2 sets a new state of the art, with at least 11% relative improvement over the previous best Mathlib semantic search engines. On top of our state-of-the-art retriever, optimized query rewriting further improves MathlibQR retrieval. On unlabeled queries from human and coding-agent interactions, Lean Finder V2 is ranked as the strongest system. Integrated with Claude Code, Lean Finder V2 improves proof success on downstream theorem-proving task. Lean Finder V2 is available at: https://leanfinder.github.io/

title: A neural-network model to find correlations in astrochemical space
authors: Daniel Giovanni Vargas, Darío Barreiro-Lage, Carlos Cabezas, José Cernicharo, Germán Molpeceres
abstract: The detection of new interstellar molecules is central to astrochemistry, and arguably the most transformative development in the field in past decade has been the increase in both number and diversity of detected species. Using natural language processing models, we develop a machine-learning pipeline, similar to other approaches reported in the literature, to connect molecular structures, encoded as chemical strings, and molecular column densities in TMC-1. The workflow generates astrochemically informed embeddings that can be employed in subsequent supervised learning tasks. These representations are used within a neural-network framework to perform column-density regression on both the original molecular inventory and out-of-distribution species. The resulting model achieves mean squared error values of 0.17/0.58 and mean absolute error values of 0.29/0.59, and coefficients of determination of 0.88/0.51 for the train+validation and validation datasets. The latent vectors learned by the model are rich mathematical objects that capture the underlying chemical relations and also the potential interstellar detectability of the molecule. Using these vectors in molecules obtained from systematic permutations of the TMC-1 inventory, we identify several promising candidates for future detection in this cloud, together with a large number of apolar species. By training the model on datasets reflecting different historical epochs of molecular detections in TMC-1, we show that recent molecular detections have substantially reshaped our understanding of interstellar chemistry, in a transformative, rather than incremental, way. Beyond accurate prediction of column-density trends for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution molecules, the latent-space representations produced by the model provide a stepping stone for developing new forms of data-driven astrochemical intuition and exploration.

title: TRIAD: Benchmarking Omni-Modal Ambiguity in Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Zhaolu Kang, Yidi Wang, Yile Li, Siqi Zeng, Yingjie He, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao hu
abstract: Ambiguity is a central feature of natural communication: a sentence, image, or sound may remain underspecified until evidence from the other channels is considered. Yet current multimodal benchmarks mostly test perception, recognition, or reasoning over already determinate inputs, leaving unclear whether omni-modal large language models can resolve ambiguity distributed across text, vision, and audio. We introduce TRIAD, a benchmark for omni-modal ambiguity resolution. Each item is a text--image--audio triplet paired with a question and a set of answer options, and is constructed so that the full triplet determines a unique answer while removing any one modality makes the set of consistent options non-unique. TRIAD contains $327$ hand-written queries in $86$ scene groups and covers $18$ ambiguity categories across the three modalities. Evaluating $14$ omni-modal systems reveals that strong item-level performance does not translate into robust scene-level disambiguation: the best model still trails humans by over $20$ points in group accuracy. Removing answer options widens the gap further, driving model group accuracy to the single digits while humans remain robust. Leave-one-out and transcript/description counterfactuals further show that current systems often underuse audio cues when text and image are present. TRIAD reframes omni-modal evaluation around disambiguation rather than recognition, and provides a taxonomy, benchmark, and diagnostic protocol for measuring this capability.

title: Discovering supernovae in the Virgo Cluster during the LSST era
authors: Jozsef Vinko, Eniko Regos, Krisztian Sarneczky
abstract: In the era of unprecedentedly wide, deep and high-cadence sky surveys the chance for discovering new explosive transients in nearby, rich galaxy clusters within hours after explosion is expected to increase dramatically. In this paper we focus on the Virgo cluster ($D \simeq 16.5$ Mpc), and estimate the expected numbers of new, very young supernovae in different sub-structures and galaxy types of the cluster during the proposed lifetime (~10 years) of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by the Vera Rubin Observatory. These predictions will be tested observationally during the ongoing Shadow-LSST discovery and follow-up program led by University of Arizona in the upcoming years.

title: A homological approach to Dax invariants
authors: Jae Choon Cha
abstract: We present a homological construction of Dax invariants in 4-manifolds that is intrinsic to the topological category and requires neither smoothing nor generic representatives. Applications include an extension of the invariant of Cha-Kim to neat disks without assuming local flatness, and a topological definition of the Dax map for arc spaces that yields a short alternative proof of the topological Dax isomorphism theorem.

title: What Ethereum Developers Ask For, and Whether They Get It: Ten Years of Ethereum Stack Exchange
authors: Tamer Abdelaziz
abstract: The Ethereum community learns where developers struggle through surveys and interviews, which record what developers say when asked about a chosen theme. Ethereum Stack Exchange (ESE) records what they ask for unprompted, and whether anyone resolves it. We study every question posted to ESE from Jan 2016 to Dec 2025, 54,637 in all, and label each with a prompt-based topic pipeline seeded with eight Ethereum-specific topics and open to new ones (22 topics in all). A three-provider committee of language models screens the labels, and manual adjudication of every disputed case puts their accuracy at 87.9 to 93.5%. Because the corpus is the complete record, no rate carries sampling error. We ask what developers ask for help with, whether the venue still resolves it, and, where it does not, whether the questions changed or their resolution did. Demand is concentrated on writing, deploying, and debugging contracts; the toolchain is the second-largest topic and growing, while security, consensus, and scaling are thin. Supply has weakened, and unevenly: answers still arrive, closure falls further. Across five estimators of the decade, the share of questions drawing any answer fell by 9.5 to 18.6 percentage points, but among answered questions the share reaching an accepted answer fell by 16.2 to 24.5. Rebuilding the later acceptance rate at the earlier topic mix moves the fall only from 9.40 to 9.32 points, so the topic mix does not explain it. Who asks separates outcomes far more sharply than what is asked: acceptance runs from 19.8% for askers below 10 reputation to 66.8% at 10k and above, a 47- point spread with a gradient in every year, against 17 across topics, and a shift toward newer askers accounts for up to 59% of the acceptance fall. The largest of seven properties an asker controls accompanies 5 points. The record places the support gap in the toolchain and among newcomers.

title: TutorCaseBench: A Case-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Tutors in Supporting Students with Challenging Behaviors
authors: Yeon Su Park, Chanyoung Park, Tae Soo Kim, Seungju Kim, Hyunwoo Kim, Daho Jung, Jinsung Yoon, Juho Kim
abstract: LLMs are increasingly used as AI tutors, yet existing benchmarks overlook the challenging behaviors common among students with learning and behavioral difficulties. We introduce TutorCaseBench, a benchmark that grounds AI-tutor evaluation in qualitative case studies from pedagogy, educational psychology, and special education. Our pipeline converts documented student categories into case-specific scenarios, tutor-student dialogues, and rubrics grounded in source evidence. The benchmark contains 923 dialogues across five challenge types, evaluated through open-ended response generation (1,560 items) and multiple-choice selection (2,537 items). Across 11 state-of-the-art LLMs, even the strongest model satisfies a rubric criterion in only 55.8% of open-ended cases, while models are better at selecting appropriate strategies than generating situated responses. These results reveal a gap between intervention recognition and context-specific adaptation, especially for open-weight models. All data are publicly available at https://github.com/kixlab/TutorCaseBench.

title: Nonlinear Drift Waves and Electrostatic Density Cavities in Upper Ionosphere
authors: Hamid Saleem, Usman Saeed
abstract: Nonlinear drift waves are investigated to explain the mechanism for the creation of one dimensional (1D) and two dimensional (2D) electrostatic density cavities in the presence of density gradient in direction perpendicular to the geomagnetic field. Ion motion along field lines has to be neglected for the formation of density depletion because nonlinear contribution of their parallel motion overcomes the effect of drift waves which create negative nonlinear potential. It is pointed out that a straightforward but appropriate model for drift waves can explain the generation of density cavities having widths in xy-plane if the external magnetic field is assumed to be along z-axis i.e. ${\bf B}_0 = B_0 \hat{z}$. The general nonlinear equation for drift waves takes the form of Zakharov-Kuznetson (ZK) equation when ion nonlinear vorticity term is ignored and it admits the solution in the form of 2D solitary wave. In 1D case, the ZK equation reduces to Korteweg de Vries (KdV) equation which admits solution in the form of 1D soliton. In both cases, the nonlinear potential becomes negative. The order of magnitude of the amplitude and width of density cavities is found to be in agreement with the satellite observations in upper ionosphere.

title: Breaking the Coupling: Efficient Concurrency Fuzzing for Linux Kernel Data Race Detection
authors: Cen Zhang, Jia-Ju Bai, Zi-Yu Zhang, Zuming Jiang
abstract: Detecting data races in the Linux kernel requires exploring both the input space and the thread-interleaving space. Existing kernel concurrency fuzzers couple these two searches by exploring interleavings during fuzzing, often spending substantial scheduling effort on inputs with little potential to trigger real races. In this paper, we present a new concurrency fuzzing paradigm that decouples concurrent-input generation from thread-interleaving exploration, enabling expensive scheduling to focus on promising inputs. To identify inputs that warrant targeted scheduling, we introduce May Race Pairs (MRPs), which represent conflicting memory-access pairs observed within a dynamically determined time threshold. Our framework first generates and executes concurrent syscall groups without controlled scheduling, collecting MRPs to guide further input mutation and identify schedule-worthy inputs. It then uses a separate scheduling instance to explore targeted interleavings and confirm real data races. To improve the effectiveness of both stages, we incorporate LLM-assisted semantic mutation for generating diverse syscall groups, backpressure-guided dynamic threshold control for balancing candidate production and scheduling consumption, and history-aware context recovery, context-aware interleaving scheduling, and candidate MRP prioritization for efficient race confirmation. We implement our framework for the Linux kernel and evaluate it on eight common kernel modules in Linux 6.17. It discovers 187 unique real-world data races, including 59 harmful races. Under the same testing budget, our approach detects substantially more data races than existing kernel concurrency fuzzers, including SegFuzz and CONZZER. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of decoupling concurrent-input generation from interleaving exploration and concentrating scheduling effort on promising candidates.

title: The ALMA-QUARKS survey: A Keplerian Circumbinary Disk Candidate in the High-mass Star-forming Region IRAS 08303-4303
authors: Gyuho Lee, Kee-Tae Kim, Tie Liu, Xunchuan Liu, Sheng-Yuan Liu, Lei Zhu, Guido Garay, Jihyun Kang, Hyeong-Sik Yun, Hong-Li Liu, Sami Dib, James O. Chibueze, Jianjun Zhou, Siju Zhang, Di Li, Pablo Garcia, Swagat R. Das, Lokesh Dewangan, Prasanta Gorai, Suinan Zhang, Aiyuan Yang, Manuel Merello, Leonardo Bronfman, Mika Juvela, Xindi Tang, Wenyu Jiao, Fengwei Xu, Zhiyuan Ren, Tapas Baug, Jihye Hwang, Patricio Sanhueza, Yankun Zhang, Xu Zhang, Chang Won Lee, Dongting Yang, Xiaofeng Mai
abstract: We present the ALMA Band 6 continuum and molecular line observations of IRAS 08303-4303, a high-mass star-forming region, with an angular resolution of $\sim 0.3''$ ($\sim 700$ au at the distance of 2.35 kpc). Six dense condensations are identified in the 1.3 mm continuum, and at least four of them are associated with molecular outflows. The estimated outflow parameters, particularly mass outflow rates $\geq 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, suggest that the driving sources are high-mass young stellar objects. Two of the condensations are forming a wide protobinary system with a separation of $\sim 900$ au. They reside within a single rotating structure, identified as a circumbinary disk which has a mass of about 2 $M_{\odot}$. This structure is traced by multiple molecular lines and exhibits a Keplerian rotation pattern. Based on the Keplerian rotation assumption, the enclosed mass is derived to be between 32 and 61 $M_{\odot}$: 22-43 $M_{\odot}$ for the primary and 10-18 $M_{\odot}$ for the secondary. The circumbinary disk is on the whole gravitationally stable, yet some parts with Toomre $Q < 2$ indicate potential fragmentation. Various molecular lines reveal a streamer-like structure connecting to the circumbinary disk, suggesting transfer of material from the envelope to the protobinary system through it. Despite the observational rarity of such circumbinary disks around high-mass YSOs, the high binary fraction among massive stars underscores their significance. This source, therefore, serves as a key laboratory for understanding the formation of high-mass binary systems.

title: A Weakly Group Strategy-Proof and Pareto-Stable Matching Mechanism with Two-Sided Indifferences under Gross Substitutes
authors: Yasushi Kawase, Ryosuke Sato
abstract: We study finite many-to-one matching markets with indifferences on both sides and publicly known firm preferences over sets of workers. A standard approach breaks ties uniformly at random and runs deferred acceptance, which is strategy-proof for workers but may select a weakly stable matching that is Pareto dominated under the agents' original preferences. For the broad class of markets in which each firm's preferences admit a gross substitutes (GS) representation, we construct a deterministic generalized deferred acceptance mechanism that is weakly stable, Pareto efficient with respect to both sides, worker weakly group strategy-proof, and implementable in strongly polynomial time given value oracles for the GS representations. This domain includes nonresponsive firm preferences, such as additive scores under matroid constraints and assignment values. Our analysis bridges ordinal matching with indifferences and competitive equilibria under imperfectly transferable utility. Although the mechanism uses only ordinal comparisons, it returns a seller-optimal equilibrium matching of a tiered auxiliary market, and the equilibrium structure of this market yields the stability, efficiency, and incentive guarantees.

title: OpenAI partially disproves Littlewood's 1961 $L^α$-flat theorem
authors: el Houcein el Abdalaoui
abstract: We present a counterexample, produced by OpenAI, to Littlewood's 1961 theorem on $L^α$-flat polynomials. The theorem asserts that no $L^α$-flat polynomials exist within the class of trigonometric polynomials of the form$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m \cos(mθ+α_m), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}^*,$$satisfying$$k\, n^2 \sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m^2 \;\leq\; \sum_{m=1}^{n} m^2 a_m^2,$$where $k$ is an absolute constant (alternatively expressed on the right-hand side as $K = 1/k$). We show that OpenAI's counterexample is contained within the class of hyper-lacunary sequences. Consequently, it offers only a limited refutation, as such sequences fail to satisfy an implicit assumption of Littlewood's theorem. We also discuss broader questions surrounding this counterexample and provide a brief historical overview.

title: GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL
authors: Shijie Li, Yilin Gao, Tieyuan Chen, Yun Luo, Weiyao Lin, Hang Yu
abstract: Training large language models for complex reasoning tasks relies on two complementary signals: sparse, outcome-grounded reinforcement learning (RL) for correctness, and dense, token-level distillation for guidance. However, complementarity in supervision does not guarantee compatibility in optimization; imitation-focused distillation can conflict with the outcome-driven RL objective, and existing hybrids lack a principled resolution. We propose \textbf{GIFT} (\textbf{G}radient-\textbf{I}nformed \textbf{F}il\textbf{T}ering for Distillation-Augmented Reasoning RL), a novel method that directly addresses the allocation problem of which teacher updates to apply. GIFT performs a token-level geometric analysis, decomposing the distillation gradient into a component \textbf{parallel} to the RL gradient, which measures first-order conflict and provides a \textbf{safety} filter, and a component \textbf{orthogonal} to it, which quantifies novel directional guidance and provides a measure of \textbf{value}. This decomposition yields a principled scoring rule to rank token-level guidance. We combine this with a progressive \textbf{coverage annealing} schedule that shrinks the budget of tokens receiving distillation, ensuring that the most conflicting updates are discarded first while the most complementary ones are retained at full strength. This facilitates a smooth transition from dense, geometrically-filtered guidance to a pure, outcome-grounded objective at convergence. Extensive experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks show that GIFT consistently outperforms strong baselines across multiple model scales, achieving relative gains of up to 9.5\% on difficult mathematical reasoning tasks. Code: https://github.com/lilifree/GIFT

title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
authors: Weiran Wang, Wenjuan Qin, Haitao Liu
abstract: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. Cross-language correspondence was greater for sociocultural meanings than for meanings concerning nature and motion, a contrast recurring across models and classifications. Within the sociocultural domain, relational differences increased with geographic separation; less closely related languages differed more across all domains. These findings suggest that universality and relativity are interwoven across conceptual domains. They inform an account in which shared cognitive resources interact with linguistic and local experience, and predict greater cross-language correspondence in human semantic judgments for sociocultural than for nature and motion meanings.

title: Report the tolerance, not the count: exact phylogenetic distance deconvolution with incomplete references
authors: Haotian Tang
abstract: Phylogenetic distance deconvolution represents mixture-to-reference distances by weighted sources placed on a reference tree. We study the minimum number of strictly interior sources that explains a distance profile, and what incomplete references cost. On a positive-rational reduced tree we give an exact algorithm with 2^O(K) poly(B) bit complexity for a free positive mean pendant and any nonempty set of observed leaves. With arbitrary missing references and a prescribed pendant the problem is W[1]-hard in the source budget K, even on positive binary trees supplied with a strict explanation using at most K+1 sources. We then use the algorithm as an instrument. Removing references can only lower the minimum source count, never raise it. The direction is a theorem at every error tolerance and held without exception in 23,545 draws, so which references are missing matters more than how many. Two adversarially chosen references suffice, at the median, to destroy uniqueness of the minimum explanation, and that number does not grow with panel size (Spearman 0.203, p = 0.15, over 20 to 353 references) where random loss scales linearly. Discarding 7,931 of 10,575 references from a real 16S panel at random costs 1.8% of the tolerance at which one source suffices. Discarding comparably many as whole clades costs 90%. That tolerance needs neither ground truth nor an error model, which makes the model measurable on real data. Published distance estimates exceed it in 296 of 296 cases. The mixture inferred by the published heuristic reproduces real observations better than the configuration that generated them in 282 of 296. The phenomenon is not unobservable in practice. It is unobservable through a point estimate of the count. Methods for this problem should report the tolerance at which an explanation of a given size exists.

title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
authors: Abdullah, Tao Huang, Ickjai Lee, Lei Bi, Euijoon Ahn
abstract: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.

title: Axial Perturbations of Extended Tolman III in the New $f(R,T)$ Theory
authors: B. N. Jayawiguna, G. A. Sabian, H. S. Ramadhan, A. Sulaksono
abstract: We investigate compact objects using the extended Tolman III equation of state in the framework of $f(R,T)=R+2χT$ gravity. In the matter sector of the Lagrangian density, we employ a new formalism based on the evaluation of the second-order derivative of the matter Lagrangian with respect to the metric \cite{Jayawiguna:2026das}. We analyze the corresponding observational signatures through axial gravitational perturbations including stellar stability and gravitational echo. We find that the effective potential in $f(R,T)$ gravity is wider and deeper than its counterpart in general relativity (GR). The quasinormal-mode (QNM) frequencies are calculated using the Bohr--Sommerfeld (BS) fitting and both the lower- and higher-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB) approximations. For the ultracompact configurations considered, trapped modes can tunnel through the potential barrier, giving rise to gravitational-wave echoes. The imaginary parts of the QNM frequencies are found to be negative, $\Im(ω_n M)<0$, indicating that the perturbations decay exponentially with time. Our results show that the echo train in GR contains more echoes than that in $f(R,T)$ gravity. Finally, assuming that the stellar object is a neutron star and adopting a stellar radius consistent with measurements by the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), we find that the $f(R,T)$ gravity model yields a characteristic frequency consistent with the estimated frequency associated with GW170817 for $β= 4.663\times10^{-1}$ and $χ=0.96π$, whereas the corresponding GR model does not exhibit comparable agreement.

title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs
authors: Chenhao Zhou, Chao Zhang, Wensong Bai, Hanbin Zhao, Hui Qian
abstract: Representation learning has substantially improved the efficiency of unconstrained continuous-state Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), but its extension to Constrained MDPs (CMDPs) is difficult because the transition representation must be learned while constraint violation is controlled. In this paper, we study representation learning for low-rank CMDPs with continuous state spaces, and propose REP-PD-TEG for the soft cumulative-violation setting. In the feature learning period, the algorithm interacts with the environment using a decaying-$ε$-greedy mixture execution policy, and uses the collected samples to learn transition features by maximum likelihood. Based on the learned features, it constructs uncertainty bonuses and plans with an optimistic Lagrangian objective to obtain the return policy. We prove regret and soft-violation guarantees for the return policies, and quantify the influence of the decaying-$ε$-greedy exploration. In particular, REP-PD-TEG achieves the optimal $\widetilde O(\sqrt K)$ return policy bound, and gives a $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ overall sample bound when exploratory actions are charged. For the stricter hard cumulative violation, where feasibility must be verified episode by episode, we propose REP-PD-H-TEG. It plans under a bonus-corrected lower-confidence utility certificate with the learned representation, and performs a stabilized dual search to obtain the return policy, yielding regret and hard-violation bounds. Together, these results give the first theoretically guaranteed representation-learning method for low-rank continuous-state CMDPs with both soft cumulative guarantees and certified hard-violation control.

title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
authors: Yiming Zhang, Jiarui Guo, Haojia Wei, Yifei Liu, Yifan Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Zhihang Zhong
abstract: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and licensed sources, with five camera instructions per scene for 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos associated with a subset of scenes. CinemaBench supports evaluation of both text-directed camera generation and video reference-directed camera generation. Across a diverse set of evaluated baselines, FilmFlow achieves the strongest benchmark performance and the highest user preference, demonstrating effective spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, and visual composition for executable 3D cinematography.

title: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability across Occupations and Countries
authors: Cristian Espinal Maya, Santiago Jiménez Londoño
abstract: 35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents in 2026, and only 2.5% can be handed over in full. Existing measures score exposure to generative AI, mostly for the United States. We build the Agent Delegability Index (ADI): two language models rate all 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements on a frozen, preregistered rubric of delegation levels and barriers; tasks are mapped to 433 ISCO-08 unit groups and weighted by ILOSTAT employment in 146 countries. Four findings. First, delegable employment rises with income, from 22.5% in low-income to 48.7% in high-income countries, a slope of 7.23 percentage points per log point of GDP per capita. This delegation divide is compositional: the physical barrier dominates the jobs poorer countries employ most. Second, at the occupation level ADI tracks exposure closely (r = 0.93 with Eloundou et al. and 0.89 with Felten et al.), above the preregistered bound of 0.80; ADI adds delegation levels and barriers on top of exposure, for the world, not a new ranking of occupations. Third, full delegation is rare and peaks for tasks that take a human about twelve minutes (11.8 minutes). Fourth, the preregistered adoption gap is not supported: across 101 countries, delegability and observed AI usage correlate at r = 0.86, and the gap between them is not wider in middle-income countries (p = 0.27). Model agreement is kappa = 0.77; a blind human rating of 300 tasks agrees with the model consensus at kappa = 0.85, and an agentic panel with web search at kappa = 0.87. We release the index, the atlas, the prompts and an MCP server at https://github.com/Cespial/delegation-divide.

title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
authors: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang
abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.

title: Probabilistic and game thresholds
authors: Rajko Nenadov
abstract: Let $X$ be a finite set and $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^X$ a non-trivial increasing property. We show that the bias-threshold $b(\mathcal{F})$ for the Picker-Chooser $\mathcal{F}$-game satisfies $b(\mathcal{F}) \ge α/ p_c(\mathcal{F})$, where $p_c(\mathcal{F})$ is the threshold for the property $\mathcal{F}$ and $α> 0$ is an absolute constant. This proves that Picker-Chooser games satisfy one-sided ``probabilistic intuition''. The proof is based on the notion of influence from the theory of boolean functions.

title: Federated Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xiaobao Wang, Renda Han, Zhiliang Xia, Meng Liu, Renxiang Guan, Di Jin
abstract: Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) leverages centralized knowledge graphs to enhance large language models with structured knowledge retrieval. However, real-world knowledge is inherently distributed across multiple organizations rather than being centrally accessible. Privacy constraints further prohibit sharing entire local knowledge graphs, preventing GraphRAG from effectively retrieving and utilizing distributed knowledge. To this end, we propose Federated GraphRAG (FedGRAG), a unified framework for distributed graph retrieval and knowledge-enhanced generation over multiple clients with knowledge graphs. Specifically, we address two fundamental challenges in federated GraphRAG. First, the absence of a global knowledge graph makes unified retrieval impossible. To address this, we develop a Federated Knowledge Routing mechanism that efficiently identifies relevant clients through lightweight knowledge indices without exposing local graph structures. Second, local graph memory cannot be shared directly because it contains sensitive entities and knowledge information. We therefore propose a controlled-disclosure evidence construction method. It extracts retrieved evidence subgraphs and converts them into an evidence abstract, enabling evidence conversion and reconstruction on the server. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Federated GraphRAG consistently outperforms existing baselines in both retrieval and downstream generation tasks, establishing a new paradigm for deploying GraphRAG in federated environments.

title: Decoherence of the quantum superradiant cloud from graviton emission
authors: Lingyun Fu, Hidetoshi Omiya, Takahiro Tanaka, Hui-Yu Zhu
abstract: Black hole superradiance amplifies vacuum fluctuations into a macroscopic cloud of a massive bosonic field around a rotating black hole. Under free evolution, the quantum cloud is a two-mode squeezed state that remains entangled even at large occupation numbers, while its growing component admits a classical statistical description. In this work, we study how graviton emission changes the quantum state of the cloud. We find that graviton emission suppresses interference between cloud configurations with different amplitudes, but leaves interference between configurations that differ only by an overall sign unchanged. For typical configurations realized under vacuum fluctuations, the suppression becomes significant when the expected number of emitted gravitons is of order unity.We also show that, at larger occupation numbers, all first and second moments can be reproduced by a statistical mixture of coherent states. For the astrophysical black holes, both changes occur much before the spin-down of the black hole becomes significant.

title: Search for high-energy neutrinos from Einstein Probe detected Fast X-ray Transients using 14 years of IceCube muon track data
authors: Sri Devaki Meduri, Shantanu Desai
abstract: We perform a time-integrated search for high energy neutrinos from 27 fast X-ray transients (FXTs) detected by Einstein Probe, using 14 years of publicly available IceCube muon-track data. We employ the unbinned maximum likelihood method which is used for IceCube point source searches. We do not find any statistically significant excess from any of the FXTs. The largest TS value is obtained for EP240801a (TS=4.77), corresponding to a local $p$-value of 0.04, which is not significant. We therefore calculate 90\% confidence level upper limit on the differential muon neutrino flux. The most stringent upper limit is obtained for EP241021a, with $E^2 Φ(E)=2.1\times 10^{-10}$ (GeV cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$), for a $E^{-2}$ spectrum at a pivot energy of 100 TeV.

title: Solvable models of learning to pursue a moving target
authors: John J. Vastola, Kanaka Rajan
abstract: Agents tasked with intercepting a moving target must learn how to reach it, ideally as efficiently as possible. As observers of animal pursuit behavior have noticed, different strategies are possible: on one extreme, the agent reactively moves toward the target's current location; on the other, the agent predicts the target's future location and moves directly there. Motivated by the desire to understand how such strategies might be learned, we introduce a continuous-time linear-quadratic model of open-loop target pursuit whose optimal control strategies interpolate between these possibilities. Usefully, a small number of interpretable parameters control which type of strategy is optimal, and it is possible to derive closed-form solutions for optimal strategies, policy learning dynamics, and value learning dynamics. Exploiting our model's linear structure, we find that the time scales of learning precisely correspond to the eigenvalues of certain matrices, and that relevant eigenvalue spectra generically have a gap. We show that this gap indicates that agents tend to learn how to reach their target before optimizing their movement. Our results provide a detailed mathematical characterization of pursuit behavior and its learning dynamics, which can both serve as a benchmark for empirical work, and as a foundation for more elaborate theoretical treatments of pursuit.

title: PhyEvolve: Multi-Agent State-Evolution Planning for Physics-Aware Video Generation
authors: Yang-Hao Zhou, Lixing Tan, Zhiqi Li, Guang Yang, Xiao Yang
abstract: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have substantially improved visual fidelity, yet existing models still struggle to understand the physical evolution implicit in user prompts, making it difficult to generate videos with continuous physical state evolution. Here, we propose PhyEvolve, a multi-agent framework that enhances natural-language prompts through structured state-evolution planning. PhyEvolve consists of three agents: a Director, a Physical Evolver, and a Composer. Given a user prompt and an optional first frame, the Director grounds the scene and disentangles physical events from observation changes. The Physical Evolver uses scene evidence to identify physical mechanisms then constructs causally linked state transitions that unfold throughout the video, whether visible or not. The Composer utilizes these transitions to enhance the original prompts. Without retraining or model modification, PhyEvolve works directly with existing generators through prompt replacement. Extensive experiments on four major benchmarks show that PhyEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the cutting-edge prior agentic baseline by 7.9 percentage points on average. These results demonstrate that explicit causal state-evolution planning improves physical consistency and state continuity in generated videos through natural-language prompt enhancement.

title: Generalized MLS and LS-SVR for Allen-Cahn Equations on Spheres
authors: Vahid Mohammadi, Mehdi Dehghan, Stefano De Marchi
abstract: This work extends least-squares support vector regression (LS-SVR) based on the generalized moving least squares (GMLS) approximation to the numerical solution of partial differential equations on spheres. We show that the proposed approach constructs a kernel-based approximant in its dual form and establishes its connection with the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Furthermore, solving the PDE through the proposed LS-SVR framework is shown to be equivalent to solving a smoothing problem or a kernel ridge regression problem in the corresponding RKHS. As applications, the method is employed to solve the Allen-Cahn equation and its conservative counterpart on spheres. An implicit first-order operator-splitting scheme is used to separate each model into linear and nonlinear subproblems. The linear subproblem is discretized by the backward differentiation formula and approximated at each time step using LS-SVR derived from a GMLS-based collocation formulation, while the nonlinear part is treated analytically. The resulting scheme is shown to admit a unique numerical solution at every time step. For the conservative Allen-Cahn model, a correction procedure is incorporated to preserve mass. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
authors: Samuel J. Ferguson, Joshua Iosevich
abstract: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

title: Finite-Query Coherent Projection of Black-Box Conditional Predictions
authors: Yuyang Wu, Fanyu Zhou, Jinfeng Zhou, Guangying Lyu
abstract: Local conditional predictions from a black box need not admit a common joint distribution. We study two aspects of their coherent projection: finite-access precision and directional fidelity. For arbitrary deterministic binary conditional tables, we establish matching expected minimax excess conditional-Kullback--Leibler risk $Θ(\min\{R\sqrt{d/B},d^2/B\})$ under independent uniform exact-table queries, with repeated draws charged, for a local bounded pairwise joint class. The result holds for sufficiently large $d$, $R\sqrt d\le M_0$, and $Cd^3\le B\le(d2^{d-1})^{1/3}$, where $M_0$ is fixed. A moment estimator attains the upper bound. The main technical contribution is a matching lower-bound construction that respects shared pairwise interactions and frozen exact-table responses, with comparison to the best projection of the same realized table. We then examine directional fidelity in a computable hard-marginal formulation that preserves direct black-box marginals. A preregistered TabPFN-v2 case study combines a Car anchor with a frozen two-dataset, three-split extension. All $1{,}152$ extension optimization instances pass independent numerical checks at registered tolerances. Directional contrasts are dataset-dependent and asymmetric: optimizing one direction need not improve the other. Together, the analyses distinguish accurate approximation of a selected projection from improvement in conditional directions outside its fitted objective.

title: Path-dependent rough differential equations in the full step-two range
authors: Xing Gao, Nannan Li
abstract: We establish the existence of solutions to path-dependent rough differential equations with non-anticipative coefficients whose regularity is formulated in terms of horizontal and vertical Dupire derivatives. Under the same regularity assumptions as in Ananova~\cite{An23}, we develop a new causal Taylor argument and establish a second-order remainder estimate. This removes the regularity loss responsible for the restriction $2\leq p<1+\sqrt{2}$ in~\cite{An23} and extends the existence result to the full range $2\le p<3$.

title: Faithful Latent Harm Monitors Work No Better Than the Models Own Behaviour at a Matched False Alarm Rate
authors: Abhishek Mishra, Sagnik Chatterjee, Suyash Maniyar
abstract: Large language models have been reported to encode the harmfulness of a request separately from their decision to refuse it, and latent safety monitors such as Latent Guard build on this report by classifying prompts as harmful from the internal activations of the model, with the aim of catching harmful intent even when the model complies. Whether these representations give a signal of harm that survives distribution shift and is independent of model behaviour is unclear. We test this on out-of-distribution prompts made by rewriting existing harmful and benign requests with surface rewording, persuasive framing and jailbreak-style wrappers. Across 15 instruction-tuned LLMs and 38 activation-based readers, we compare harm detection with that of TF-IDF and sentence-embedding classifiers, with independently trained safety classifiers, and with the refusal of each model. Activations are read at the last token of the user instruction, where the model has read the whole request, and at the last chat-template token before the reply, where the planned response can be represented. Because models disagree about which prompts to refuse, we can separate a signal of the harmfulness of the prompt from a signal of the refusal decision of the model. At the end of the instruction, the representation is largely independent of the refusal behaviour of each model but degrades under distribution shift, so that a TF-IDF classifier ranks harm better than the original Latent Guard in every model we test, and linear and MLP probes do about as well as sentence-embedding classifiers trained on the same examples. The representation just before generation detects more, catching 44 percent of harmful prompts at a matched false-alarm rate against 32 percent for the refusal of the model, but that gain follows the refusal decision itself, and part of it comes from refusals that string-matching evaluation misses.

title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
authors: Cristian Anghel, Rares Stan
abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$. The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $ν=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $ν\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $ν\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $ν\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.

title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
authors: Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Priyanka Deswal, Ethan Berger, Nicholas C. Bristowe, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
abstract: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades. Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between. The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics. In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.

title: On Modified Newton Methods for Unconstrained Optimization Based on Lanczos Tridiagonalization
authors: Aban Ansari-Önnestam, Anders Forsgren, Philip E. Gill
abstract: For a strongly convex unconstrained minimization problem, Newton's method with a line search offers rapid convergence to a minimizer by incorporating second-order information. However, for a general unconstrained problem the Hessian need not be positive definite, which can lead to the inability to find a search direction or to search directions that fail to produce descent. Modified Newton methods are designed to handle this situation. This paper considers modifications to a Newton-conjugate-gradient approach based on Lanczos tridiagonalization. Existing methods are extended using dynamic modification schemes that provide a descent direction while keeping the modification bounded. A Lanczos-based scheme and a conjugate-gradient (CG)-based scheme are formulated and analyzed. These methods are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, but their practical behavior differs in finite precision. Finally, it is shown how the convergence and computational cost are affected by varying the amount of additional curvature introduced and by allowing the early termination of the inner iterations.

title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
authors: Joseph W. Abbott, Paolo Pegolo, Pol Febrer, Michelangelo Domina, Sandra Saade, Matthias Kellner, Filippo Bigi, Philip Loche, Michele Ceriotti
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches or improves on the released reference models at lower inference cost and, compared with equivariant models, a smaller memory footprint. The predictions give accurate IR and Raman spectra and isotropic shieldings; the predicted densities accelerate self-consistent field calculations and give one-shot ground-state properties, and pretrained density models transfer to higher levels of theory by fine-tuning on little data. The impact of approximate equivariance is small for most observables, further validating this approach to train fast, accurate, and useful surrogate models for properties beyond the PES.

title: Exceptional point structure and chiral state transfer in a rate-operator-engineered $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Bose-Hubbard dimer
authors: Jaakko Luomala, Federico Settimo, Kimmo Luoma, Iiro Vilja, Jyrki Piilo
abstract: The rate operator quantum jumps (ROQJ) is a general method to unravel a master equation describing the dynamics of an open quantum system into stochastic pure state trajectories. By post-selecting on no jumps occurring, one obtains a trajectory generated by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The ROQJ allows for versatile modification of this non-Hermitian evolution, with each non-Hermitian Hamiltonian corresponding to a different continuous measurement scheme. We apply the ROQJ to modify the non-Hermitian dynamics of the open three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer model under environmental non-local dephasing to construct a $PT$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with a general two parameter $PT$-symmetric imaginary diagonal part, which generalizes the well-known gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. We characterize the symmetry structure of the spectrum for different on-site interaction strengths. For vanishing on-site interaction, we find the unbroken $PT$-symmetry region enclosed by order two exceptional lines of different character and four order four exceptional points, two of which are not found in the usual gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. Additionally, we find regions with degenerate imaginary parts of the eigenvalues, also not found in the gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. In this parameter space, we use time-dependent rate operator transformations to investigate state transfer under slowly varying parameter loops. Loops encircling an order four exceptional point exhibit chiral state transfer. Because the loops cross exceptional lines, the final states are superpositions of eigenstates. Chiral state transfer is also found with non-zero homogeneous on-site interaction when the loop crosses over broken $PT$-symmetry regions of different character. Using inhomogeneous on-site interactions, we find direction dependent state transfer between eigenstates without crossing or encircling exceptional points.

title: A recurring changing state AGN discovered in the SAMI Galaxy Survey and SDSS
authors: Scott M. Croom, Rebecca McElroy, Dougal Dobie, Thomas Dunn, Yasmeen Janschek, Tyler Klinger, Shaun Parasher, Mitchell Spanner, Oliver J. Thorp
abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the AGN in galaxy J085337.26+014303.6 at z=0.0582. A combination of SDSS and SAMI Galaxy Survey data shows that this object has gone through at least one full changing-look AGN cycle, from type 1.9 in 2001 to type 1 in 2015 and 2021, and then type 1.9 again in 2022. While the broad lines in this object show evidence of dust obscuration, detailed spectral analysis plus WISE photometry demonstrate that the changes in this object are related to a physical state change, not changing obscuration. In fact, the WISE light curve suggests that this object may have briefly returned to a type 1.9 state in 2020. In the optical, the host galaxy dominates the light (e.g. only ~10 per cent contribution from the AGN at 4000 Angstoms within a central aperture), even in the high state. In contrast, the brightest WISE W2-band measurements place the AGN at a similar luminosity to the entire host galaxy. The broad Balmer lines show evidence of multiple components, with a weak very-broad component (FWHM=5000-6000 km/s) visible in the low type 1.9 state, and a stronger broad component of FWHM~2000 km/s dominating in the high type 1 state. We propose that this is caused by two spatially distinct regions within the broad line region.

title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
authors: Anirban Basak, Shaibal Karmakar
abstract: For a $Δ$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{Δ/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $Δ\geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In contrast, for $Δ=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erdős-Rényi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{α^*_H/(α^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $α^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

title: Stability-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneity-Aware Composite Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control
authors: Jichen Zhu, Chaopeng Tan
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a flexible mechanism for adapting traffic signal control to heterogeneous traffic and sensing conditions, but directly learned signal actions do not automatically inherit the analytical properties of structured traffic-control methods. This paper proposes Com-MP, a theory-guided RL framework that learns a context-dependent composition of multiple max-pressure (MP) control preferences while retaining decentralized MP phase selection. The learned policy adapts the relative influence of constituent MP formulations according to local traffic and sensing conditions, allowing data-driven adaptation to operate within a structured traffic-control framework. We show that such intersection-specific and time-varying composition preserves strong queue stability for every demand in the strictly stabilizable region under any admissible non-anticipative composition policy, thereby separating the performance-adaptation role of learning from the stability property of the underlying controller. In a representative implementation combining detector-supported queue-based MP and connected-vehicle-supported travel-time MP, experiments on a real-world 45-intersection network show that Com-MP reduces average delay by 15.6\% and 8.6\% relative to the two constituent controllers, respectively, and by about 7.0\% relative to the best fixed composition. The learned composition responds systematically to local traffic and sensing conditions, remains effective under heterogeneous and degraded sensing, and can be transferred without retraining to an unseen network with an average delay only 2.4\% higher than that of a policy trained directly on the target network. These results show how learning-based adaptation can be introduced within a stability-preserving traffic-control structure, providing a theory-guided pathway toward trustworthy learning-enabled traffic signal control.

title: Learning Low Modes of the Wilson Dirac Operator with Gauge-Equivariant Networks
authors: Minjae Choi, Hiroshi Ohno
abstract: In adaptive multigrid, test vectors that better approximate the low-mode subspace of the Wilson Dirac operator $D$ can reduce the solve time, but their construction can be costly. In some cases, the setup takes longer than a single solve. To reduce the cost of generating test vectors, we train networks built from gauge-equivariant parallel-transport layers once on a quenched ensemble, using a Rayleigh-Ritz loss for $D^\dagger D$. We then test whether the trained networks maintain their performance at other hopping parameters and on configurations not used in training. In these tests, the network outputs are used as test vectors, and the costly $V$-cycle refinement in the adaptive setup is omitted to reduce the setup time. This substantially reduces the setup time while leaving the solve time largely unchanged in most cases. Near the critical hopping parameter $κ_c$, the solve time is also reduced in some cases.

title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
authors: Ava Pun, Kevin Dai, Sally Chen, Maxwell Jones, Ruixuan Liu, Kangle Deng, Changliu Liu, Maneesh Agrawala, Deva Ramanan, Jun-Yan Zhu
abstract: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling.
