The comparison changes judge-training objective as well as response format, and the main ranking is conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result. A limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.

title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
authors: Leming Shen, Qiang Yang, Xinyu Huang, Zijing Ma, Yuanqing Zheng
abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.

title: On $C^2$ circle diffeomorphisms with rotation numbers of constant type
authors: Junhao Li, Lin Wang
abstract: For every irrational rotation number $α$ of constant type and every $q>1$, we construct a $C^2$ circle diffeomorphism $F$ arbitrarily close to the rigid rotation $R_α$ in the combined $C^2$ and $B^2_{2,q}$ topology whose normalized conjugacy is not Lipschitz. We also prove that $F''\in B^0_{2,1}$ implies global $C^1$ conjugacy. Thus the thresholds in the Besov summability and weak Dini scales are $q=1$ and $γ=1/2$, respectively. These results complement Herman's Baire category theorem on the residual existence of $C^2$ diffeomorphisms without $C^1$ conjugacy by providing quantitative counterexamples and sufficient conditions for differentiable conjugacy.

title: Strain Waves Generate Compression and Trigger Buckling in Active Polymers
authors: Wen-de Tian, Kang Chen, Tianhui Zhang
abstract: Chemical reactions can sustain polymer motion without necessarily generating the compression required for buckling. Theory and simulations show that tension-dependent chemical transitions coupled to bond elasticity generate finite-wavelength traveling strain waves in a semiflexible polymer. In the straight chain at fixed axial span, the waves reduce mean active contraction while leaving mean elastic tension unchanged, generating compression that drives bending above a threshold. Releasing the mean load allows longitudinal waves to persist while transverse perturbations decay.

title: Demand-Driven Routing Space for Lattice-Surgery Compilation
authors: Hanyu Wang, Wan-Hsuan Lin, Zihan Chen, Eddy Z. Zhang, Jason Cong
abstract: Lattice-surgery compilation places logical qubits on a grid of surface-code tiles and routes their interactions. Sparse static layouts limit routing contention but reserve space that often remains idle. Reducing this reservation requires balancing area savings against additional gate serialization and qubit movement. In this paper, we present a co-designed dynamic architecture and compiler that allocates routing space according to circuit demand. The architecture preserves a fixed virtual qubit floorplan while allowing its physical spacing to change between execution stages. The compiler coordinates placement, scheduling, and routing to implement lattice surgeries using fewer physical qubits. Across our application benchmarks, our method reduces space-time volume by 55.6% in geometric mean and compiles 75.5 times faster than the evaluated DasCot configuration. A circuit-synthesis case study shows how our compiler exposes optimization tradeoffs.

title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

title: Where Did the Light Come From? Diagnosing Cast-Shadow Reasoning in VLMs and Borrowing the Missing Shadow Prior from Image Generation Models
authors: Ryugo Morita, Shunsuke Kitada, Stanislav Frolov, Brian Bernhard Moser, Ko Watanabe, Riku Takahashi, Jinjia Zhou, Andreas Dengel
abstract: Shadows are observable consequences of latent physical causes, arising from the interaction between illumination, object geometry, and scene structure. A model that understands shadows should be able not only to read a shadow's direction, but also to infer where a shadow should fall when it is absent, and to judge whether a shadow is physically consistent with the scene. We introduce ShadowBench, built from real photographs, which poses these three questions to vision-language models (VLMs). From each scene, we build a correct-shadow, a shadow-removed, and a human-annotated wrong-direction state. Evaluating 19 open VLMs (2B to 78B) and frontier proprietary models, we find that VLMs read a visible shadow's direction well above chance and improve with scale, yet infer the absent direction only weakly and fall to chance at judging physical consistency even under a bias-free two-alternative test that removes the yes-bias of single-image naturalness questions. Only Gemini-3.1-pro exceeds chance on validity, and even then only modestly and far below humans. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) does not help. The missing ingredient is not reasoning but knowledge that image generation models (IGMs) already hold. Routing a VLM through an IGM lifts its inference well above its direct attempt and helps it flag the wrong-direction shadows it otherwise accepts. Cast-shadow direction is a single facet of illumination understanding, but the sharp gap it reveals between VLMs and IGMs suggests image-generation or reconstruction objectives as a route toward illumination-aware VLMs.

title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
authors: Jie Ying, Xutao Zhang, Ningyuan Chen, Mengce Zheng, Jun Li, Zhongjie Zhu, Tiantian Zhu
abstract: When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing. Runtime overlays normalize native observations, while a deterministic pipeline joins invocation and result lifecycles, constructs a typed provenance graph, selects a policy-decisive slice, and binds claims to recorded evidence. Given the same normalized trace, overlay version, and pre-run policy oracle, the diagnosis can be recomputed and its claims re-checked without language-model judgment. Across five runtimes, one contract captures all 159 applicable executions, with an audit of native and synthesized identifiers. On 120 adjudicated cases, AgentTriage achieves 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate, improving joint diagnosis by 0.175 (95% CI [0.092, 0.258]) over the strongest same-schema baseline. These results quantify the precision of replayable diagnosis and the observation boundaries that require abstention. We release an open-source implementation and selected sanitized evidence at https://github.com/AsnGs/agenttriage-open-source.

title: Matter Induced Bounds: Photon Ring, Lyapunov Exponent, Induced Temperature
authors: Hocheol Lee, Bogeun Gwak
abstract: We investigate analytic bounds on the equatorial photon ring radius and the Lyapunov exponent in rotating black holes containing anisotropic matter. For a constant equatorial equation-of-state parameter, the finite asymptotic mass and nonnegative energy density imply an upper bound on the photon ring radius given by the Kerr photon ring radius with the same asymptotic mass and rotation parameters for co-rotating and counter-rotating motions. The lower bounds are written in terms of the quantities evaluated at the outer horizon. These bounds on the Lyapunov exponent constrain the absolute magnitude of the imaginary part of the quasinormal frequency of a massless scalar field within the eikonal limit. The worldsheet surface gravity and induced temperature were derived for a probe string in the Penrose limit along the photon ring. The induced temperature and worldsheet surface gravity give an upper bound on the photon ring Lyapunov exponent, $2 πT_\mathrm{ind} = κ_\mathrm{ind} \geq λ$.

title: SmolVLA-MoE: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
authors: Shiyang Zhang, Miao Yang, Zhengda Li, Yang Shao, Ruifang Zhai, Hui Peng, Peng Song
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in multi-task robotic manipulation by leveraging visual and language understanding for action generation. However, existing lightweight VLA models employ a single dense action expert to handle all tasks, which limits their multi-task capability under constrained computational budgets. To address this issue, we propose SmolVLA-MoE, a novel framework that introduces sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) into the FFN layers of the action expert in VLA models. SmolVLA-MoE replaces dense FFN layers with multiple parallel expert FFNs and a token-level router, enabling each token to adaptively select the most suitable expert for action generation. We further introduce a shared expert with a tunable weight parameter to balance the inheritance of pre-trained capabilities and task-specific expert specialization. Through sparse activation, SmolVLA-MoE activates only a single expert FFN during inference, with a total activated parameter count of approximately 500M including the frozen VLM backbone, while benefiting from approximately 800M total stored parameters. We evaluate our method on four task suites of the LIBERO benchmark. SmolVLA-MoE achieves an average success rate of 84.25%, outperforming SmolVLA (82.75%) and OpenVLA-7B (76.5%), while maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/dudu435/smolvla-moe.

title: Symmetry-Preserving Local Representation for Short-Range Interaction in Complex Materials
authors: Hao Cheng, Tong Yang, Hao Wu, Haokai Hong, Zhongrui Wang, Shu Ping Lau, Wanyu Lin, Kay Chen Tan, Ming Yang
abstract: Modeling short-range interactions in highly disordered materials remains challenging due to the immense configuration space and the disruption of local symmetry in truncated theoretical models. Here, we propose a symmetry-preserving local representation framework that strictly enforces topological continuity and translational invariance via boundary passivation. Applied to high-entropy alloys, this approach autonomously unravels the nonlinear ligand effects modulating local reactivity and accurately captures coverage-dependent many-body interactions without explicit periodic expansion. By resolving the conflict between localized chemical environments and extended periodic boundaries, this framework not only reduces computational complexity by an order of magnitude but also provides a physically transparent paradigm for deciphering short-range order in complex condensed matter systems.

title: From Natural Language to Verified C: Verification-Guided Generation with ACSL Specifications
authors: Zian Wang, Qin Li, Weisong Sun, Haibin Cai
abstract: AI-assisted code generation amplifies the demand for automated formal verification. Generated programs must not only be executable but also accompanied by machine-checkable evidence of correctness. Existing approaches can synthesize functionally plausible code or plausible-looking specifications from natural-language prompts; however, they do not explicitly co-design the implementation and specification as a unified artifact optimized for verification. Consequently, automated verifiers often fail to discharge proof obligations. Typical failure modes include missing or implicit proof anchors, program structures that are hostile to automated reasoning, and inconsistencies between code-level state and specification-level requirement facts arising from the independent generation of code and specifications. Even when verification succeeds, it may only establish weak specifications that omit requirement-critical behavior. This paper introduces VeriGen-C, a formal-verification-friendly framework for the joint synthesis of C programs and ACSL specifications from natural-language requirements. Code generation and repair are constrained to expose proof-relevant state, to streamline control flow for deductive verification, and to eliminate implementation patterns that hinder automated proof search. Specification generation and refinement are similarly constrained to mitigate verification timeouts and to ensure alignment with the user requirements. Empirical evaluations on HumanEval-X, FM-Bench, and LiveCodeBench Lite demonstrate that VeriGen-C substantially improves the rate of verified and requirement-aligned solutions relative to an interface-compatible baseline, from 5.5% to 44.5%, from 44.3% to 80.0%, and from 6.5% to 58.7%, respectively.

title: On adjoint double shuffle relations and adjoint reduction relations
authors: Takumi Anzawa
abstract: In this paper, we give a positive answer to Jarossay's question under the adjoint reduction relations. Namely, we prove that the extended double shuffle relations together with the relation $\!\!\!\mod π^2$ are equivalent to the adjoint double shuffle relations together with the adjoint reduction relations.

title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
authors: Yuan Si
abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]

title: Estimating Group Average Treatment Effects in High-Risk Populations with Unobserved Target Membership
authors: Shubo Zhang, Yinjun Zhao, Donglin Zeng, Yuanjia Wang
abstract: Estimating treatment effects within a prespecified high-risk population is challenging. When risk status is unobserved or the target population is small, analyses restricted to high-risk individuals can be unstable or inefficient. We propose a risk-score-weighted soft-targeting (RSW) estimator for group average treatment effects in high-risk populations. It accommodates two settings: when high-risk status is observed, the membership probability can be estimated within the analysis sample; when unobserved, it can be obtained from a reference model using covariates in the analysis sample. RSW uses these probabilities to represent the target population, learns a doubly robust treatment effect in the full sample, and aggregates a low-dimensional treatment-effect surface over the risk-weighted target distribution. We establish pointwise asymptotic normality and an influence-function-based variance estimator. In simulations with continuous and binary outcomes, RSW had similar bias and lower variance than two hard-targeting alternatives. Sensitivity analyses showed that the gain persisted when treatment-effect sufficiency was violated, although RSW bias increased under strong violations. We applied the method to the All of Us study to estimate effects of non-GLP antidiabetic and antihypertensive medication use on mild cognitive impairment (MCI)-free time restricted at 48 months within comorbidity-defined high-risk subgroups. We estimated the risk score in a nonoverlapping internal reference sample and applied it to the outcome-analysis sample. This illustrates how soft targeting can improve precision while retaining an interpretable high-risk target population.

title: Hidden Convexity of the Joint Range of Three Quadratic Forms and Applications
authors: Tuan Ngoc Hoang, Huy Quang Nguyen
abstract: We investigate a hidden convexity phenomenon for triples of homogeneous quadratic forms. We give a complete characterization of the convexity of the upper image obtained by adding the nonnegative orthant to their joint range. More precisely, the upper image is convex if and only if either a nonzero nonnegative linear combination of the three associated matrices is positive semidefinite, or the three quadratic forms admit a common strict negative direction. In particular, the upper image is convex whenever one of the three quadratic forms is convex. As applications, we establish the convexity of an associated value function and derive a generalized S-lemma for implications involving two quadratic inequalities and a strict theorem of the alternative for quadratic systems.

title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
authors: Yang Liu, Zhiqiang Yuan, Shu-Dong Huang, Jiancheng Lv, Liwei Yang, Qiwei Yan, Kailin Lv, Jinchao Zhang
abstract: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.

title: In-Orbit Computing for Remote Sensing: Task-Oriented Processing and Transmission
authors: Yi Zhang, Zesong Fei, Jingxuan Huang, Hua Dang, Jihao Luo, Wenyu Liang, Haoran Zhang, Xinyi Wang
abstract: The growing volume and timeliness requirements of remote sensing data are exposing the limitations of the conventional "transmit-then-process" architecture, particularly under intermittent satellite-ground connectivity, constrained downlink bandwidth, and limited onboard computing resources. This article presents a semantic-aware space-ground collaborative remote sensing (SSGC-RS) framework, in which remote sensing data are processed to different semantic depths according to task requirements and available communication-computing resources. Three operating modes are considered, ranging from fully onboard task inference to semantic representation delivery and space-ground split inference. A land-cover recognition case study illustrates how these modes address different communication and computing bottlenecks. Finally, emerging challenges and future directions for intelligent remote sensing systems are discussed.

title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
authors: Ai-Jun Li, Qingzhong Huang
abstract: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}Φ''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $Φ(t)+(s/n)tΦ'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overlineΦ(t)=\int_0^tΦ(τ)\,dτ/τ$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.

title: Learning Domain Trajectories with Flow Matching for Gradual Domain Adaptation
authors: Yubo Huang, Yushe Cao, Zixi Wang, Jingzehua Xu, Xin Lai, Xiongyu Hu, Shuai Zhang
abstract: Large distribution shifts remain a primary obstacle for domain generalization and unsupervised adaptation. Although gradual domain adaptation alleviates this difficulty by introducing ordered intermediate domains, most existing approaches still operate in a discrete, step-wise manner, which can accumulate errors and often relies on unstable Min--Max optimization. We propose \textbf{FlowGDA}, a flow-matching framework that models gradual adaptation as \emph{continuous} transport on a statistical manifold in a representation space. FlowGDA learns time-dependent velocity fields that induce smooth domain trajectories, using a simulation-free regression objective rather than adversarial training. To prevent semantic drift, we couple left-to-right transport between consecutive domains with a source-anchored transport and a semantic consistency loss, and we further stabilize learning via a two-stage sequential optimization scheme. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, validating flow matching as an effective alternative for domain adaptation.

title: Direct cueing of word identity through word duration: evidence from Mandarin homophones
authors: Xiaomeng Zhu, Megan Niu, Jason Shaw, Kevin Tang
abstract: While there is increasing evidence that words are stored in the mental lexicon with some phonetic detail, there are open questions about exactly which phonetic details are stored and whether they are functionally relevant for spoken word recognition. Word-level phonetic cues, such as word duration, provide an appropriate test case. Across languages, including Mandarin Chinese, high frequency words are shorter than low frequency words. Using a homophone ordering task, we investigate whether differences in word duration impact word recognition. Mandarin Chinese was examined since it has abundant disyllabic homophones. Our results indicate that participants were able to use word duration to recognize the order of homophone pairs, selected to vary in lexical frequency. Both with high noise levels and when no other cues were available, participants mapped the shorter duration auditory stimulus to the higher frequency word. The results provide evidence that word duration can directly cue the identity of words, suggesting that it may be a phonetic detail incorporated into the lexical representation. We discuss this direct cueing account alongside alternative accounts of how word duration may modulate word recognition.

title: Early panchromatic spectra reveal helium in the thermonuclear supernova 2024kce
authors: Abigail Polin, Dillon Hasenour, Sahana Kumar, Willem Hoogendam, Jing Lu, Daniel Polin, Danielle Dickinson, Braden Garretson, Nidia Morrell, Huei Sears, Katie Auchettl, Teresa Boland, Christopher Burns, Kenneth C. Chambers, Dhvanil Desai, Jason T. Hinkle, Thressay Hoover, Eric Hsiao, Mark E. Huber, David O. Jones, Colin Macrie, Bailey Martin, Cameron Pfeffer, Miranda Pikus, Benjamin J. Shappee, Madeline Taylor, Brad E. Tucker, Michael Tucker, Huangfei Xiao
abstract: Faint Type I supernovae blur the boundaries between spectroscopic classes, obscuring their progenitors and explosion mechanisms. One proposed origin is a double detonation, in which ignition of an accreted helium shell triggers the explosion of a carbon oxygen white dwarf. Surviving helium is a direct prediction of this mechanism, but its strongest near-infrared feature overlaps with carbon and is ambiguous in isolation. Here we present SN 2024kce, observed with simultaneous optical and near-infrared spectroscopy eleven days before maximum light. We identify He I absorption at three wavelengths, all consistent with a velocity of 16,400 km/s, well above the photosphere. This is the first detection of helium before maximum light in a thermonuclear supernova. Helium at these velocities requires nearby radioactive material for non-thermal excitation, pointing to ash from a detonated surface helium shell. A double detonation model reproduces the optical spectral evolution, suppressed blue flux, and He I 1.083 micron absorption feature. SN 2024kce shares properties with both subluminous Type Ia supernovae and Ia-like calcium-rich transients, providing evidence that the same explosion mechanism operates across these classes. From early optical and near-infrared spectra to Rubin's First Look images, SN 2024kce showcases the full reach of modern observatories in exposing the physics of rare explosions.

title: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure for Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems
authors: Fudu Xing, Kailong Wang, Tianlong Yu
abstract: LLM-based scam systems increasingly combine adaptive dialogue, persistent context, external tools, and multi-agent coordination to automate personalized fraud. These capabilities also create a resource dependency: every reasoning step, model call, and coordination round incurs inference cost. We present TokenTrap, a resource-oriented defense that redirects suspected scam systems toward benign, low-value computation while withholding credentials, payments, and other exploitable information. TokenTrap combines three components: an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that selects among single-agent, hierarchical, and flat multi-agent workflows, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation while enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits. Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by $2{,}487.0\times$, $1{,}616.0\times$, and $567.8\times$ relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.

title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
authors: Ying Han, Yuan Tian
abstract: Atomic-scale strain governs the electronic, ferroic and mechanical properties of materials, and atomic-resolution microscopy measures it most directly. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) is the standard tool, but it fails when a Bragg reflection moves outside its fixed Fourier aperture under large strain or rotation, or in misoriented grains. Here we introduce geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA), whose Fourier aperture tracks the Bragg reflection at each pixel in real space. A narrow aperture can therefore reject noise without losing a displaced reflection. On 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images under various imaging conditions, GPTA reduces GPA's failure rate from 27% to 11.5% with up to 335 times better accuracy. It also gives strain and dislocation maps across grains, resistance to dynamical-scattering extinction, and a confidence map, capabilities that GPA lacks. Tracking the aperture combines reciprocal-space dose efficiency with real-space spatial resolution and extends atomic-scale strain metrology to beam-sensitive materials and challenging imaging conditions.

title: On a finite group in which every non-nilpotent maximal invariant subgroup of order divisible by $p$ is normal
authors: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li, Na Li
abstract: Let $A$ and $G$ be finite groups such that $A$ acts coprimely on $G$ by automorphisms. For any fixed prime divisor $p$ of $|G|$, we prove that if every non-nilpotent maximal $A$-invariant subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ is normal then $G$ has a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.

title: Sharp convergence rate of the estimation error of LASSO via the Feature Space Decomposition method
authors: Guillaume Lecué, Zong Shang
abstract: In this paper, we use the Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) method to establish an explicit, non-asymptotic, instance-optimal convergence rate for the estimation error of the LASSO in the Gaussian linear regression problem for any signal, any diagonal covariance and any regularization parameter above $σ_ξ/\sqrt{N}$ where $σ_ξ$ is the noise variance and $N$ the number of data.

title: GSHeadRelight: Fast Relightability for 3D Gaussian Head Synthesis
authors: Henglei Lv, Bailin Deng, Jianzhu Guo, Xiaoqiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Di Zhang, Lin Gao
abstract: Relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits are essential in applications such as portrait photography, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). Despite recent progress, 3D-aware portrait relighting remains challenging due to the demands for photorealistic rendering, real-time performance, and generalization to unseen subjects. Existing works either rely on supervision from limited and expensive light stage captured data or produce suboptimal results. Moreover, many works are based on generative NeRFs, which suffer from poor 3D consistency and low real-time performance. We resort to recent progress on generative 3D Gaussians and design a lighting model based on a unified neural radiance transfer representation, which responds linearly to incident light. Using only in-the-wild images, our method achieves state-of-the-art relighting results and a significantly faster rendering speed ($\times12$) compared to previous 3D-aware portrait relighting research. Project page: http://www.geometrylearning.com/GSHeadRelight/.

title: Mode-Selective Micromotion Compensation via Coherent Excitation of a Ground-State-Cooled Motional Mode
authors: Tetsu Kinase, Ippei Nakamura, Atsushi Noguchi
abstract: Excess micromotion induced by stray DC electric fields limits the control fidelity of trapped-ion experiments. Various techniques have been developed to detect and compensate ion displacements from the RF null by monitoring modulated fluorescence, ion positions, or micromotion sidebands. Although these approaches are effective, they do not probe the displacement through a ground-state-cooled motional mode and therefore offer limited compatibility with quantum-enhanced sensing protocols. Here, we demonstrate a micromotion compensation method based on the driven coherent amplitude of a ground-state-cooled motional mode. In this approach, the ion displacement is converted into a coherent motional excitation by an auxiliary RF drive and detected through the qubit. We determine the optimal compensation field with a $1σ$ statistical uncertainty of 8 mV/m. The method is naturally compatible with quantum-enhanced sensing protocols employing nonclassical motional states, including Fock, squeezed, and Schrödinger-cat states, providing a pathway toward quantum-enhanced micromotion compensation.

title: Asymptotically Sharp Length Thresholds for \texorpdfstring{$q$}{q}-ary Codes with Distances \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2} and \texorpdfstring{$4$}{4}
authors: Valjakas Djaljapayan, Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Wei-Hsuan Yu
abstract: For an integer $q\ge5$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of a $q$-ary Hamming space of length $n$ in which every two distinct words have distance $2$ or $4$. Set \[ N(q)=\left\lceil\max\left\{2q+1, \frac{17+\sqrt{8q^2+96q-95}}2\right\}\right\rceil. \] We prove that $A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2$ for every $n\ge N(q)$. In particular, $N(q)=2q+1$ for $q\ge26$. An explicit code of size $q(n-2)$ shows that the least eventual threshold $N_*(q)$ satisfies $N_*(q)\ge2q-1$; consequently $2q-1\le N_*(q)\le2q+1$ for every $q\ge26$. The argument applies to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, without a linearity assumption. Its main ingredients are synchronization of symbols on intersecting supports, weighted bounds for $2$-intersecting families of four-sets, and a joint estimate for the weight-two and weight-four layers in a common-three-core configuration. No computational verification is required.

title: Better Reasoning, Not Just Bigger Models: A Structure-Grounded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Inference
authors: Amirhossein Aghaei, Liangyan Li, Shiyi Yang, Shaohua Wang, Yan Wang
abstract: Scaling large language models has substantially improved linguistic fluency, yet reliable autonomous agents require more than fluent generation. In multi-turn inference, current agentic systems often produce semantically plausible but structurally ungrounded reasoning, especially under incomplete observations. We propose Structure-Grounded Uncertainty Reduction (SGUR), a training-free framework that complements token-level generation with active uncertainty reduction over structured hypothesis spaces. SGUR represents incomplete observations as a query graph and aligns them with candidate hypothesis graphs through a prior-weighted partial graph matching mechanism, where database-derived empirical priors assign greater importance to decision-relevant relations rather than treating all graph edges uniformly. The resulting inference state is iteratively refined by an active information-gain strategy that selects the next most informative node to query, systematically pruning the candidate space. We instantiate SGUR on a challenging PrimeKG-derived sequential medical diagnosis benchmark, demonstrating that structural grounding can partially substitute for model scale: starting from only two observed symptoms, SGUR achieves 92.5% Hit@3, outperforming the strongest Graph-RAG baseline by 9.4 percentage points while using approximately 5x fewer tokens. Notably, SGUR enables smaller backbone models to match or exceed the performance of models up to 10x larger, suggesting that structural grounding provides a more robust and efficient paradigm for scaling agent performance than relying exclusively on increasing model size.

title: Impacts of generative AI skill development on academic adaptation and learning outcomes among university students
authors: Lei Fan, Fangxue Liu
abstract: Understanding how university students perceive the development of their generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) skills over time can clarify how GenAI use relates to learning and academic outcomes. This study examined perceived skill-development trajectories, changes in learning practices, and associated academic gains using a retrospective questionnaire with 313 analyzed responses and interviews with 18 students across subject areas. Descriptive and comparative analyses and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were integrated with thematic analysis. Perceived developmental trajectories were heterogeneous: 34.2% of students reported rapid early improvement followed by a plateau, 28.4% steady improvement, and 21.1% delayed acceleration. Development was also uneven across skills, with improvement in evaluating GenAI outputs perceived as more challenging; assignments were the most frequently selected driver of skill growth. Interviews further indicated increasingly specific prompting, tailored verification, and selective delegation, although some students reported stable routines, dependence, skipped reasoning, or improvements attributable partly to better GenAI tools. Academic gains were reported more often for assignments than for examinations. The SEM indicated a positive indirect association between perceived skill growth and academic gains through adaptation of assignment processes, whereas academic gains did not clearly differ across developmental trajectory groups after multiplicity correction. The findings suggest that perceived GenAI skill development varies in both trajectory and skill domain and is associated with changes in learning practices and differentiated academic benefits.

title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
authors: O. Bystrenko, B. Ilkiv, S. Petrovska, O. Foia, T. Bystrenko, O. Khyzhun
abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. The examination of electronic structure indicates that, in contrast to the conventional h-BN, which is an insulator with the wide band gap, the predicted orthorhombic phase is expected to be a semiconductor with the narrow band gap of ~ 0.65 eV.

title: TT-SAX: A Two-Track Time Series Symbolization for Natural Language Shape Querying
authors: Zhao Tan, Xianglong Bao, Zhipeng Xi, Ming Jin
abstract: Natural language querying for time series databases aims to let users find what they need in long histories of data by asking in plain language. Shape queries ask how a series moves. They are the main challenge of this task. Recent work makes them feasible by using symbolization as a bridge between the query and the long history. However, existing symbolizations were designed for compression, similarity indexing, or classification. What a symbolization should provide for natural language querying has not been systematically studied. We therefore examine the definitions of six classical symbolizations against this task and identify three limitations. (1) Direction is missing from the string, (2) direction is measured at too small a scale, and (3) the letters are arbitrary. Three design principles follow. We follow these principles and make a minimal redesign of SAX called TT-SAX (two-track SAX). The level letters stay. Each segment gains a trend letter. It is measured across neighboring segments rather than inside one, and graded to match the adjectives that queries use. We conduct extensive experiments on the public NLQTSBench benchmark, comparing TT-SAX with the six classical symbolizations across six LLMs. TT-SAX outperforms all six on shape queries, and ablations trace its gains back to the three limitations one by one. This paper is the first systematic study of time series symbolization with natural language querying as the design goal. It provides a foundation for future research on this task. Our code is available at https://github.com/Atlamtiz/tt-sax.

title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
authors: Shaolin Ji, Xinmeng Liu
abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: CoRE: Relating Fine-Grained Chest X-ray Findings in Anatomical Context
authors: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon
abstract: Chest X-ray interpretation depends on both the anatomical location of findings and their relationships with other abnormalities. However, relations defined over global finding labels do not explicitly distinguish the same finding across anatomical locations. We propose CoRE(Co-occurrence-guided Region Evidence), a framework that incorporates relationships among findings and anatomical context into fine-grained chest X-ray prediction. It groups anatomical region-finding labels by co-occurrence and uses these groups to guide shared representation learning through visual prompt tuning on a frozen vision transformer. The predictions are supplemented by an anatomically supervised region-evidence stream through region-matched logit residuals. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR with Chest ImaGenome annotations show that CoRE improves region-finding classification over standard and relation-aware prompt-based baselines. Quantitative evaluations on MS-CXR and the Chest ImaGenome gold standard show improved finding localization, supported by qualitative comparisons. CoRE also improves finding-level classification on mapped finding labels in external VinDr-CXR and CheXpert datasets without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate the value of jointly modeling finding relationships and anatomical context for fine-grained chest X-ray analysis.

title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
authors: Katsuhiko Higuchi, Masahiko Higuchi
abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by ${}_S\langle Ψ| \hatψ(x)\hatψ(x') | Ψ\rangle_S$, where $|Ψ\rangle_S$ is the superconducting state, and where $\hatψ(x)$ is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al.\ regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J.\ Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

title: DagFlow AI: Agentic Synthetic Data Generation for Personalized Statistics Learning
authors: David Arthur, Ranjini Grove, Zaher Kmail, Curtis Atkisson
abstract: To provide personalized learning experiences in courses that teach data analysis skills, instructors often search for datasets that appeal to a student's interests, align with specific learning objectives, and are appropriate for the student's skill level. Datasets that match all three criteria can be difficult to find. DagFlow-AI is an agentic AI data generation tool that creates realistic, synthetic datasets tailored to these criteria. Rather than mimicking existing datasets or generating observations directly, DagFlow-AI uses the broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to specify the components of transparent, reproducible data-generating mechanisms from which observations are generated programmatically. We illustrate how the tool can be used to construct a realistic, synthetic dataset and describe how it aligns with both the Guidelines for Assessment and Instruction of Statistics Education (GAISE) and the Problem, Plan, Data, Analysis, and Conclusion (PPDAC) framework for teaching data analysis

title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
authors: Xinke Xing, Yixuan Yang, Xinzhi Zheng, Renhong Gao, Li Deng, Jintian Lin, Ya Cheng
abstract: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.

title: Deep-Learning Identification and Global Characterization of Energetic O2+ Beams at Mars
authors: Chi Zhang, Chuanfei Dong, Kathleen G. Hanley, Yaxue Dong, Hans Nilsson, Eduard Dubinin, Jasper Halekas, Janet Luhmann, Shannon Curry, Jiawei Gao, Yilan Qin, Xinmin Li, Hongyang Zhou, Liang Wang
abstract: Martian ionospheric ions can be accelerated away from Mars by the solar wind, contributing substantially to atmospheric ion escape. Here, we develop a U-Net-based image segmentation model to identify a distinct population of escaping planetary ions, energetic O2+ beams, from a decade of Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) observations and perform an event-based statistical analysis of their global properties and dependence on external conditions. We find that O2+ beams are widely distributed throughout the Martian plasma environment, with a strong preference for the +E hemisphere, where the solar wind convective electric field points away from Mars. This pronounced spatial asymmetry indicates that the convective electric field plays a major role in beam formation. In the solar wind and magnetosheath, these beams are consistent with the plume. Their occurrence-weighted flux agrees with previous long-term plume estimates, whereas the flux during identified beam intervals is substantially higher. This highlights the advantage of our event-based approach in capturing the intrinsic properties of O2+ plumes. In the induced magnetotail, beam formation remains strongly associated with the convective electric field, while the Hall electric field can provide additional energization. The beam properties are primarily controlled by upstream solar wind conditions, with no apparent influence from solar extreme ultraviolet irradiance. These results might improve our understanding of ion escape at Mars. More broadly, we also demonstrate the potential of deep learning for identifying transient plasma populations from spacecraft observations.

title: Bridging the Closed-World Gap: Interpretable Anomaly Detection via a Hybrid TSK-FCM Ensemble on the BETH Dataset
authors: Lohith Srikanth Pentapalli, Josette Riep, Justin Ouwerkerk, Kelly Cohen
abstract: A fundamental paradox plagues the deployment of Machine Learning in cybersecurity: supervised models generalize poorly to novel, Out-of-Distribution (OoD) attacks, whereas unsupervised models often suffer from poor separability, leading to unmanageable false-alarm rates. This challenge is exemplified by the BETH dataset, a kernel-level benchmark in which the training data consists solely of benign and suspicious insider behaviors, whereas the test set consists almost entirely of novel botnet activation attacks. To bridge this detection gap, we propose a Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble that synergizes the precision of supervised learning with the adaptability of unsupervised clustering. Our architecture integrates a gradient-optimized Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy classifier to act as an expert on known insider threats, with a parallel Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) module to detect geometric anomalies. A critical finding of our research is that traditional fuzzy membership scores degrade in high-dimensional feature spaces due to the curse of dimensionality. We overcome this by introducing a robust Min Distance metric that exploits the raw geometric isolation of botnet activation attacks. This approach yields a state-of-the-art AUROC of 0.9951 on the BETH test set, outperforming the original Isolation Forest baseline by 17.1%. By combining near-perfect OoD detection with the intrinsic interpretability of fuzzy logic, our framework offers a viable path toward robust, transparent, and autonomous network defense.

title: Stale Instruction Files Override the Code in Coding Agents: A One-Sentence Fix
authors: Xiaonan Xu, Wenjing Wu
abstract: Purpose: Coding agents follow a project's instruction file, such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, even when it disagrees with the existing code and even when they notice the disagreement. We measure this behaviour and test whether one sentence in the user's own instruction file makes agents follow the code instead. Methods: We built 40 Python projects in which the instruction file asks for one convention while the existing code uses another, for example print instead of logging. Claude Code and Codex CLI added a feature to each project, with and without a sentence in the user-level instruction file that gives the existing code precedence, in 320 runs. Results: Without the sentence, 90.1% of the agents' choices followed the stale file. Claude Code pointed out the conflict in 79 of 80 runs and still followed the file. Codex CLI rewrote the existing code to match the file in 20 of 80 runs, and the project's own tests then failed in 17 of them. The sentence raised the share of choices that follow the code from 4.2% to 91.4%, stopped the rewrites and raised the test pass rate from 89.4% to 100%. Conclusion: We attribute the behaviour to how agents receive the two sources: the instruction file reaches the model as an instruction and the code as tool output, which models are trained to rank lower. Users can add the sentence today, and makers of agents and models can build the same rule into their products.

title: Exact Characterization of Admissible Bandwidths for Linear Disturbance Observers
authors: Hamin Chang, Hyuntae Kim
abstract: This paper characterizes the entire set of admissible Q-filter bandwidths, equivalently parameterized by the time constant $τ$, that guarantee robust internal stability of a linear disturbance observer (DOB) under parametric plant uncertainties. Classical small-$τ$ stability results provide a rigorous foundation for Q-filter bandwidth design. Building on this foundation, we formulate the $τ$-dependent robust internal-stability problem as a semialgebraic feasibility problem in bivariate polynomials and prove that the complete admissible set is a finite union of open intervals under the standing assumptions. A constructive procedure with exact membership tests recovers all stabilizing intervals. A numerical example with an uncertain plant family containing non-minimum-phase members illustrates a disconnected admissible set.

title: Multiplicity Distribution in the Color Glass Condensate Formalism
authors: H. R. Martins-Fontes
abstract: The multiplicity distribution (MD) of charged particles in high-energy proton-proton collisions remains an intricate aspect of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Traditional models, such as the Negative Binomial Distribution (NBD), were fitted and successfully described MDs at lower energies, but fail at higher energies, such as those probed by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), where a ``shoulder-like'' structure emerges. To address this, we employ the Double Negative Binomial Distribution (DNBD), a weighted combination of two NBDs, representing contributions from soft and semi-hard processes. This model typically involves six free parameters, but by incorporating the $k_T$ factorization formalism and introducing an energy scale $Λ$, we effectively reduce the number of free parameters from six to four while maintaining a strong fit to high-energy MD data. The unintegrated gluon distribution used in this work is derived from the Golec-Biernat-Wüsthoff (GBW) model. Additionally, we investigate the KNO scaling and use the $k_T$ factorization formalism to describe the pseudo-rapidity distribution. Our approach demonstrates excellent agreement with recent experimental data, yielding low $χ^2$ values and highlighting the potential for improvements using more realistic gluon distribution model. This analysis provides valuable insights into the interplay of soft and semi-hard processes in high-energy collisions.

title: Repair Changes Which Layers to Remove: Exact Optima for Depth Pruning of Language Models
authors: Jianchang Su, Dawei Xiang, Yifan Zhang, Wei Zhang
abstract: Depth pruning removes entire transformer layers to make large language models faster, and recent methods recover quality by replacing the removed layers with a training-free linear map. Which layers to remove, however, is chosen with heuristic scores whose distance from the best choice is unknown. We evaluate every subset of layer groups exactly (about 53,000 pruned models across four families, with and without repair) and find that the best layers to remove depend on the repair: linear repair absorbs the interaction among nearby layers and turns the optimum from a split layout into a contiguous block, so methods that choose layers without the repair miss the repaired optimum by up to 189%. We therefore select layers under the repair that will be applied. A greedy search at the cost of SLEB lowers perplexity by 20% to 66% relative to ReplaceMe on five models up to 27B parameters, and with a task objective it is up to 25 points more accurate given the same data. A second-order expansion of the loss yields a score that selects the repaired block from one forward and one backward pass of the intact model.

title: Half-Completeness from Standard Gravitational Dispersion Relations
authors: Lukas W. Lindwasser, Laurentiu Rodina, Justinas Rumbutis
abstract: The completeness hypothesis states that quantum gravity realizes every representation allowed by its gauge group. Previous S-matrix arguments used the graviton pole to constrain exchanged representations, including a proof of completeness by imposing an additional high-energy bound on crossing-odd amplitudes. We investigate what follows without this assumption, using standard twice-subtracted dispersion relations, positivity, and crossing symmetry. For external massless SU(2) isospin $J$, we prove ``half-completeness'': either massive exchanges include every isospin $j\le J$, or at least one $j>J$ is required. At $J=1$, we construct an explicit amplitude with only $j=0,1$ exchanges that satisfies these conditions but violates the crossing-odd bound. This establishes that the additional high-energy assumption does not follow from the standard framework. For $J\ge2$, however, we show that lower-only spectra cannot be realized within a class of string-inspired Euler amplitudes, leaving their existence an open question. More generally, for scalar matter transforming under any compact internal symmetry group, we prove that massive singlets of unbounded Lorentz spin must be exchanged.

title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
authors: Sy-Tuyen Ho, Anirudh Satheesh, Soham Chawathe, Huy Nghiem, Yongkyun Lee, Andrew Adams Schoen, Furong Huang
abstract: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
authors: Sachin Gupta
abstract: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu, Kai Zhang, Jiemin Fang, Qi Tian
abstract: Single-image 3D generation has achieved high fidelity on curated benchmarks, yet degrades sharply on real-world images with uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions. Purifying such inputs requires deciding when to intervene and preserving the visual cues needed for 3D generation, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. We introduce Gate3DGen, a selective pre-processing model that gates image inputs to existing 3D generators without retraining them. A degradation-aware router bypasses inputs classified as clean and extracts features to guide purification of the remaining inputs. Conditioned on these features, a 3D-oriented one-step purifier purifies degraded inputs with spatial losses that encourage preservation of object identity, contours, and textural cues. To provide paired supervision, we construct a synthetic data engine that renders clean views of 3D assets and synthesises composite degradations. On the synthetic benchmark, the purifier improves image fidelity and downstream 3D geometry in only 2.3s on average, reducing TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% relative to degraded inputs. VLM evaluation and human preferences on real photographs further support identity preservation and degradation correction. More demos and code are available at https://supra-3d.github.io/gate3dgen.

title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
authors: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
abstract: Monocular models recover 3D geometry from a single image in one pass, but most assume a pinhole camera and produce distorted geometry on the wide-angle imagery produced by fisheye and panoramic lenses. Camera-aware models remove this assumption by predicting a per-pixel ray field. However, they represent different camera geometries using a single fixed basis to capture both the overall camera projection and its finer variations. We argue that camera geometry can be viewed as having a hierarchy of complexity for representing rays. We present OmniRay, a feed-forward model whose Ray Module is composed of three components: a monotone radial base that captures radially symmetric structure, a spherical-harmonic residual for smooth deviations from it, and a free-form residual for remaining local variation. These components are composed as successive rotations on the sphere, allowing the representation to accommodate diverse camera geometries. Given a single image, OmniRay predicts a ray direction and an up-to-scale radial distance for every pixel, from which a 3D point cloud is recovered without needing camera information at inference time. Extensive experiments across different camera configurations demonstrate that OmniRay establishes a new state-of-the-art in camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.

title: UniVOE: A Removal-Driven Framework for Interaction-Aware Universal Video Object Editing
authors: Shuzhou Yang, Lanqing Guo, Lingen Li, Weiqi Li, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo, Jian Zhang
abstract: Video object removal and injection are reciprocal editing operations between object-present and object-absent video states, yet they differ substantially in training difficulty. Removal can be effectively bootstrapped from video inpainting and further adapted to erase object-related interaction effects. Injection, however, requires large-scale paired supervision to model object appearance, dynamics, and scene-dependent effects, while perfectly aligned real-world pairs are difficult to collect and synthetic data lacks sufficient realism and diversity. To address this challenge, we present UniVOE, a removal-driven framework for training both video object removal and injection models. We first train an effect-aware remover by transferring video inpainting priors and finetuning on object-present/object-absent pairs. The trained remover converts real object-present videos into object-absent counterparts, creating large-scale paired supervision for injection. An injection model is trained on these pairs in the reverse direction to recover objects together with their dynamics and interaction effects. Moreover, since pixel-level reconstruction alone cannot adequately capture perceptual realism, we introduce a reward-based post-training method that aligns injection results with human preferences using a proprietary reward model. Experiments against strong open-source and commercial systems demonstrate that UniVOE achieves state-of-the-art performance on both object removal and injection, particularly in challenging interaction-effect cases.

title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
authors: Gabriele Dominici, Teague McMillan, Fazl Barez, Marc Langheinrich, Martin Gjoreski
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.

title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
authors: Alexander Meiburg
abstract: Does computing a composition of total Boolean functions require the product of the randomized query complexities of its factors? We give a negative answer. There are families of total functions $f,g$ such that $R(f\circ g) =Θ\!\left(\frac1{\log R(g)}\right)R(f)R(g)$ This result requires first separating linearized query complexity $\LR$, as well as noisy randomized query complexity $noisyR$, from standard randomized query complexity $R$. Both constructions essentially come from totalizing existing partial function separations, albeit via different techniques. By adapting these techniques, we also construct total functions separating every adjacent pair in the chain from sabotage $RS$, max-conflict $\barχ$, and linearised query complexity $LR$. We show that AND-of-ORs separates conflict $χ$ from max-conflict $\barχ$ complexity and makes conflict and sabotage incomparable. Finally, randomized complexity can be smaller than its composition limit $R^*$ by the maximal factor $Θ(\log R)$. The total--total composition separation is also formalized in Lean.

title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
authors: Marek Šuppa, Ivan Vykopal, Jaroslav Kopčan
abstract: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated. We use an LLM once, as a corpus debugger rather than a classifier: a tool-using agent explores the corpus through a read-only, budgeted API and compiles each finding into an executable test, which a native speaker then validates. On the 26.5M-document Slovak portion of FineWeb2, three runs costing \$2.21-\$2.84 each found seven findings over four phenomena. The largest is a machine-generated content farm of 1,408,437 documents (5.32%) that passed the pipeline's filters, 86.6% of it passing even stricter thresholds. Blinded labels support 6 of the 7 findings (defect rates .53-1.00 against .08 in a random control) and do not support one. The compiled suite scans the full corpus in 0.7 s of wall-clock time without a GPU, against \$12k-\$90k per LLM classification pass. The best static sampling baseline validates more selectors than any agent run, at under half the cost. The agent contributes exact prevalence, a precision estimate checked against sampled documents, an account of why the pipeline missed each slice, and a reusable test. We release the framework, Slovak test suite, validation data and agent trajectories.

title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
authors: Jacques L. Pienaar, Eran Tal, Asya Ciftci
abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

title: Ray-by-Ray: Fine-Grained Resource Management for GPU Ray Tracing Units
authors: Junrui Pan, Cesar Avalos Baddouh, Kai Ze Ee, Timothy G. Rogers
abstract: Ray tracing (RT) generates photorealistic images by simulating the physical behavior of light as it interacts with surfaces in a virtual scene. In film production and high-end rendering pipelines, this technique computes global illumination, reflections, refractions, and soft shadows by tracing millions of light rays per frame and accurately modeling their bounces and attenuation. Contemporary GPUs incorporate specialized ray tracing hardware to accelerate key operations in the traversal pipeline. By accelerating these stages in hardware, the unit enables real-time ray tracing for complex scenes that previously required offline computation. However, ray tracing introduces substantial control and data divergence. Each ray may traverse a different set of nodes in the acceleration structure, encounter distinct materials, or terminate at varying depths. This irregularity reduces thread coherence and exposes a fundamental disparity between the GPU SIMT and per-thread execution model of dedicated RT units, where each ray progresses independently. In this work, we seek to validate assumptions made in open-source infrastructure and identify potential inefficiencies in resource management within the ray tracing pipeline. To address inefficiency caused by mismatches between SIMT and RT granularities, we propose Ray-by-Ray, which decomposes on-chip buffers into the granularity of individual rays and introduces lightweight management structures that enable more warps to run in parallel without increasing buffer capacity. This approach improves ray tracing unit utilization and increases memory-level parallelism. Experimental results show that Ray-by-Ray achieves an average performance improvement of 1.91x over the baseline, with an area overhead of 0.19\%.

title: DiffDreamer: Coupling World Models with Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control
authors: Fanxing Li, Yuxiang Huang, Shengyang Wang, Fangyu Sun, Shuyu Wu, Tianbao Zhang, Dexin Zuo, Yan Yufei, Danping Zou, Wenxian Yu
abstract: Tasks such as quadrotor dynamic-gate racing require agents to anticipate external motion while maintaining precise high-frequency control. World-model-based reinforcement learning provides a natural solution by learning latent dynamics for future imagination, yet it often entangles environmental evolution and the robot's own dynamics in a single learned rollout, where model bias can affect policy optimization efficiency. We propose DiffDreamer, a differentiable reinforcement learning framework that tightly couples a learned world model with differentiable simulation for actor optimization. In one optimization step, the learned world model propagates latent states that capture external dynamics and history-dependent features, while the differentiable simulator propagates the robot's explicit physical state. We further decompose the actor objective into a critic-driven pathway for non-differentiable task rewards and a simulator-driven pathway for differentiable motion rewards. Experiments on aggressive tracking and dynamic-gate racing show that DiffDreamer improves training convergence over the model-free, model-based, and differentiable-RL baselines, and final performance over these baselines and classical planning and control methods. Additional experiments assess reward decomposition and the odometry-conditioned relative-state representation through ablations. We also provide proof-of-concept real-world flight experiments for validation.

title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
authors: Johannes Girsch, Robert Kurinczuk
abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},μ_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
authors: Atiksh Bhardwaj, Edward W. Duan, Junwon Seo, Prithwish Dan, Wei-Chiu Ma, Andrea Bajscy, Preston Culbertson
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its execution?} Our method trains linear probes on policy activations from demonstrations to estimate progress, then flags executions that deviate from expected progress. In experiments with the open-source VLA $π_{0.5}$ and across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, this approach is competitive with or outperforms VLM-based monitors in task failure detection, as well as methods which require failure data for training. These findings suggest that simple probes of VLA internals can be used to develop reliable runtime monitors, opening a path toward building policies that can act reliably and monitor their execution without external foundation models.

title: Nonconformal kinetic theory with transverse dynamics and event-by-event simulations using CoMBolt-RTA
authors: Seyed Farid Taghavi
abstract: A new version of CoMBolt, called CoMBolt-RTA, is introduced to solve the Boltzmann equation for massive quasiparticles in the relaxation time approximation (RTA). The inclusion of a constant quasiparticle mass allows one to obtain an equation of state (EOS) closer to that of lattice QCD.
